In this retelling of Dante's origin story which is set against a contemporary backdrop, DmC Devil May Cry™ retains the stylish action, fluid combat and self-assured protagonist that have defined the iconic series but inject a more brutal and visceral edge.
The Dante of DmC is a young man who has no respect for authority or indeed society in general. Dante knows that he is not human, but also that he is not like the demons that have tormented him throughout his life. Caught between worlds, he feels like an outcast.
Thanks to his twin brother Vergil, leader of the anti-establishment group called “The Order”, Dante is now discovering and coming to terms with what it means to be the child of a demon and an angel. This split personality has a real impact on gameplay with Dante being able to call upon angel and demon abilities at will, transforming his Rebellion sword on the fly to dramatically affect both combat and movement.
For DmC Capcom has teamed up with UK development studio, Ninja Theory, renown for delivering action titles with compelling characters and narrative coupled with high production values. The combination of Ninja Theory’s expertise and Capcom’s unrivalled heritage in producing combat focused action titles will ensure that this latest addition to the over 11-million selling series will remain true to the Devil May Cry DNA so cherished by the fans, while bringing a new level of cinematic quality to the title.

Joking aside, my first impression was quite annoying from a technical side, and especially unexpected from an indie game. It doesn't give you the choice of whether to upload gameplay stats to the official server. And unlike almost all games I ever played, it doesn't instantly recognize a firewall block, so first you'd have to wait roughly a minute at game start and then it spoils the gameplay by frequently popping up another error message window about not being able to contact the server, as if this was a catastrophe. Hell, I didn't even access the stats list. (When playing it recently, it didn't bug me during gameplay again.)
The only workaround is to not only put Steam in offline mode (which is pseudo-offline), but to also disconnect from the internet.
Or accept the idea that a paying customer doesn't deserve to make decisions like this and face the consequences of that corporate-style mindset.
Gameplay-wise, I don't understand what all the fuss about the allegedly frustrating difficulty is. Maybe I'm oldschool because I grew up with NES (e.g. I never found the 'infamous' Mission Impossible as difficult as claimed), but all you have to do is accept that the game is meant to be that difficult and you can die over and over without getting frustrated. It's good practice. I suspect people are just not used to that anymore these days with all the pampering going on. Dying is not the end, haha. In this game it is mostly void of negative consequences, and it is a very good design decision to allow you to restart a failed attempt almost instantly. Just one key press and you're ready for the next try.

TL;DR: This game is worth every penny, ignoring the bundle price and the trading cards.
Well, BEEP may look simple, it is VERY CHALLENGING in the later levels. The concept is simple, and so are the controls. There are tips here and there so you won't be wondering what the hell you are supposed to do. Though, in some part of the game, you can take the unconventional (and easy) way to collect those anti-matter nuggets.
The game has amazing physics, even with unusually shaped objects. The combat system (morea accurately, aiming system) is also simple. Your crosshair locks onto targets and you can shoot like a pro while you jump here and there. There's that infinite ammo thing (you have to reload though, either by right clicking on your robot or by pressing "R") so you don't have to worry about missing a shot. You have an antigravity beam which allows you to move objects (even enemy corpses) and you will feel the incredible physics this game is offering. You robot's wheels have a good grip and you won't slip off edges easily.
Now coming to the graphics and music. Everything is cartoon-ish, and the music is electronic blip blop type. I personally like both of them but many people hate these type of things. It's upto one's own aesthetics.
The game interface is simple. TOO SIMPLE. You don't get to tweak any type of settings. You can't change the volume, you can't modify your save files and so on. This is basically the only side of the game that I hate.
The game has trading cards, adding badges, backgrounds and emoticons, adding another layer of variety.
Overall, this is a solid game.

Bear in mind I've only played a specifically short time. But having played a couple levels I feel as though I've seen the very basics of what the game has to offer.
If you're into silly platformers or you have kids that are into silly platformers, BEEP is worth checking out. Definitely a childish art style for a game that still holds enough challenge to have the ability to hold an adult's interest. It's very light and goofy, unlike almost every other game I enjoy. If you want to skip your gore for a night, BEEP is a great choice. Being 1.99, you can expect to get about two dollars of enjoyment from it. It's the same price as going to the dollar store and getting a soda and a bag of chips. But I tend to finish my food rather quickly and finish games rather slowly, so beep will definitely be enjoyable long after my snacks are gone. If you REALLY want a cheeseburger right away, BEEP can wait. But if you happen to have a couple bucks to spend and nothing else sparks your interest, you might want to pick it up and give it a try.

This game is just incredible. For the price, it is a bargain even when not on sale. I've been playing it since the early access release. The depth of the simulation is ground-breaking and much more complex and satifying than games in the Tropico franchise, which is perhaps the closest example. The game works because of fun gameplay. But its genius is in the AI - which is both simple and elegent, because the individual prisoners, workers and guards all respond to each other. You don't really control them. They do things within the environment you give them and they will interact with each other on their terms, sometimes violently. Watching the prison life has kept me hooked for hundreds of hours.
Despite the fun cartoon graphics, this game is serious in the themes it tackles. It simulates the business model of running a private prison. You can be a real♥♥♥♥♥♥in this game, just like many real-world private prison operators. The more extreme you play and the more corners you cut, the more conflict will arise between prisoners and guards. There are so many factors that determine what happens in your prison - resentment grow, fights break out sporadically and can escalate over time into protests, riots and full blown prison rebellions. You can keep striving to make things better for the prisoners, or clamp down on them. Repression works. Except when it doesn't. Total rebellion is the best thing to watch play out. I love this game because it shows how power and authority are never complete or total even in a controlled environment like a prison. Your rule can be undermined, resistance can escalate and all hell can break loose when people are denied basic life needs and pushed too far. Get this game and break rules, play evil. Do nasty stuff to see what happens, you won't regret it.

Depending on if this is your first Batman game, this game has two separate reviews.
Like with all the other Batman games, the storyline is well written. The villians add a lot of substance and most the time do not come off as simple cameo time. The voice acting is exceptional and diverse. When dealing with the street thugs however, their dialog repeats way to often. You will constantly hear about the guys making fake ID's to do a bank job... Don't worry because he is a professional "and he never make mistakes!"
Graphics are top notch just like every other Batman game. And this is where the differences in rating start to change. If you are new to the series, the graphics are easily outstanding. As you go through the game, your suit, to include your cape develops damage showing just how much the Batman does in a night. If you are a verteran, this is the same as all the other games and the only difference is that the detail is a little more polished. Overall, the graphics have not taken much of an increase. In fact, the small extras floating around the city (like papers and trash) are less. The spark effects have been increased through. One thing I can say however is that this game has a lot more graphical glitches in it than the others.
Next is the storyline. If this is your first Batman, the story is pretty stable. The ending will leave you fealing left out as though they did not finish the game and just ended it. Which was actually the point as this is the prequal to the first game. So those who have played the other two will enjoy how everything ended up and know exactly what is going to happen next.
As far as the controls are concerned, If you are again new to Batman, the controls are very fluid and easy to use. Some of the moves are not completely explained and hope you have experience with the other games to know their full capability on how and when to use them. If you are a veteran, the controls at times seam a bit sluggish at times.
One thing I hated about the second game was the Riddler puzzles. The first game made the chalenges insightfull and semi reasonable. The second game just tried to make them as difficult and annoying as possible. The Riddler had his  own optional storyline but was truly annoying to complete. The third game however toned chalenges down and added a bit to the optional storyline.
Overall, the game is excellent for new and old players and should be picked up. Considering this is an origins story, you can play this one either first or third.

Ori and the Blind Forest is one of those rare few games which leave a lasting impression that remains long after you've finished. The story, while simple, is heartwarming and illustrated beautifully. Every region you pass through is gorgeously illustrated. And the soundtrack ties everything together with splendid, magically immersive music.
Be warned, though, the gameplay is quite challenging - your adorable little forest spirit is going to die many, many deaths falling on beds of spikes, being crushed under rocks, getting killed by enemies, vaporizing to death lasers, and more. However, that should not be confused with gameplay that is punishing. You can create your own save points whenever you are not in any imminent danger, and in most cases, deaths cause only a marginal setback. Many difficult areas can be done section by section, allowing you to learn from each death and slowly master the platforming.
Ori and the Blind Forest will not be a leisurely stroll through a peaceful woods - you are out to save a world that will take any opportunity it has to snuff your little light out. But anyone up for the challenge will be treated to an amazing world and adventure, a touching story, and an outstanding game.

In this retelling of Dante's origin story which is set against a contemporary backdrop, DmC Devil May Cry™ retains the stylish action, fluid combat and self-assured protagonist that have defined the iconic series but inject a more brutal and visceral edge.
The Dante of DmC is a young man who has no respect for authority or indeed society in general. Dante knows that he is not human, but also that he is not like the demons that have tormented him throughout his life. Caught between worlds, he feels like an outcast.
Thanks to his twin brother Vergil, leader of the anti-establishment group called “The Order”, Dante is now discovering and coming to terms with what it means to be the child of a demon and an angel. This split personality has a real impact on gameplay with Dante being able to call upon angel and demon abilities at will, transforming his Rebellion sword on the fly to dramatically affect both combat and movement.
For DmC Capcom has teamed up with UK development studio, Ninja Theory, renown for delivering action titles with compelling characters and narrative coupled with high production values. The combination of Ninja Theory’s expertise and Capcom’s unrivalled heritage in producing combat focused action titles will ensure that this latest addition to the over 11-million selling series will remain true to the Devil May Cry DNA so cherished by the fans, while bringing a new level of cinematic quality to the title.

I am greeted with what sounds like a wrestling comentator yelling 'SUPER MEAT BOY', but this contrasts to the rest of the game. The game can be quite relaxing and also quite tense, as anyone who has completed a boss battle will know. You play as Super Meat boy, and you have to complete platformer tasks to get to your love, who has been stolen by Dr Fetus (whose trading card is badass in a photo). This is the kind of game in which you die a lot, sometimes hundreds of times in one level; although, I have never enjoyed dying so much as I do in Super Meat Boy. You respawn instantly, and the amount of deaths do not matter at all to your score or completion of the game.
I reccommend Super Meat Boy. I do not play many Indie games, but I love this game. If you play a lot of Indie games, I dare say you will love this game even more.

Super Meat Boy makes me want to punch both of the developers in the face a lot for coming up with something that makes me cuss and die more than anything since Megaman in the NES days.
Mashing down on the keys so hard you feel like you're about to punch through your laptop as you repeat the same mistakes with minor difference to the last time that buzzsaw, laser, rocket-thing, gap of doom got you.  Finally overcoming that challenge and finding the most minor obstacles just sent you back to the beginning again to fail some more.
But... those dopamine hits you get when you run that brutal, skinless gauntlet and succeed makes you want to love and hug those two nerdy guys from Indie Game: The Movie.
Bravo, you sadistic programmers of wonder!
For giving us the lovable characters of Meat Boy, Bandage girl and Doctor Fetus.
For putting us in touch with the inner-masochist that we never knew was there.
For producing something more addictive than crack with a slightly decreased detriment to our health and longevity.
For making this vegetarian genuinely love Meat again...

What the game did well:
High level of car customizability means no two cars will be alike. However aside from the engine and armour, it's not customizability, but rather upgrading, as the next version is objectively better.
Good graphics.
Good sound.
Combat system is a fluid and fun melee brawl where you have light and heavy attacks and have to counter the enemy attacks.
The place felt like a wasteland. I could see the rusting wrecks of ships, oil refineries, left over detritus like plastic dumps, etc. It was mostly empty, raider attacks weren't that common, and considering the amount of land the game stretches over, there weren't that many enemies.
I really felt like danger was around every corner, because there was, although the enemies were kind of easy (Except for the enemies who grapple you, ♥♥♥♥ those guys.)
There was actually a reason to stick to the road. For example, you play an open world game like Skyrim and often it's far more efficient to just go in a straight line to the destination rather than follow the roads. Whereas in Mad Max you go really slow on rocks and sand until you get good wheels, and even then it's still faster to just go on the road.
What I didn't like:
At the beginning of the game it seems to make a big deal out of the scarcity of fuel and water. But then you get on the road and not only is there usually about 50% of a canteen at every scavenging location and a full one in camps, but I was literally DROWNING in fuel. Like you go in a camp and immediately you see like 10 cans just lined against the wall! And then there are many more scattered throughout the place. And it takes about 5 hours of solid driving IRL time to actually empty your car's tank, so fuel is worthless.
I think it's stupid that an action game about beating gangs of raiders to death and death races and crashing your car into an enemies car causing mutual death and death death death you are rewarded for sitting around doing nothing. While you have to cause plenty of death to get these passive scrap aquiring resources, once you get a few of them rolling you're getting far more scrap passively than actively. Just so you know you get 20 scrap every like 20 minutes for every camp you have, and there is a stronghold upgrade that gives you like 1 scrap per 5 minutes offline. So say you deck out all your fortresses like this, go to bed, and then you wake up 8 hours later with an extra 100 scrap! Then you wait a few minutes and you've got hundreds more! Meanwhile you clear out a Top Dog camp, get like 100 scrap, clear a scavenging location, get 50.

First off, the only feature I loved about the game was character creation.  So many options and the ability to adjust things to your liking without having to use presets, which I assumed a game like this would.  (Judging by the graphics and how similar the characters look.) Now once I finished and chose my spawn location, I was pretty excited about getting into the game.  Once I loaded, the first thing I noticed right off the bat was the graphics were less pleasing to the eye than they were during character creation. You're immediately given tutorial quests which basically give you the run down on controls and game basics, but I was shot and killed before I could even finish the second list.  Apparently you have the option of being or not being ready, and your decision effects whether or not another player (real person, not npc) can come and shoot you, bash into your car, or any other way to ♥♥♥♥ you and your♥♥♥♥♥♥up.  I'm not sure when I became ready, was probably just an accidental setting I did while being a derp with the keyboard commands, but I wish that would have been earlier in the tutorial lists so that I would know "Hey don't go outside while you're ready or some random will see your noob♥♥♥♥♥and kill you on sight."
I was then asked to hijack a car and drive 500m.  First, I had to hit the F key 3 times before my character would even consider the possibility of taking a car, and it took me a few times to finally hijack one because by the time I hit the F key enough times, the vehicle was driving off and my character was just standing there in the middle of the road being the prissy little♥♥♥♥♥♥she's been since the start. is a top-down simulation game like the ages-old Tycoon games on PC. You're tasked with overseeing all aspects of prison management. The developer,
, truly has thought of everything in this regard, too. You build the prison from the ground up, lay water pipes and electrical wiring, hire staff like guards, doctors, and therapists, install surveillance and emergency countermeasures, and if you eventually have the prison running as it should, then you have to keep it that way.
This is done by keeping the population of inmates fed, content, nonviolent, and within the walls and fences of the institution. Because you're also operating a private prison, the endgame is to also make money.
The introduction to the game's many systems can be extremely intimidating at first. Thankfully, this feeling of being overwhelmed is largely undone using the game's Prison Stories mode that doubles as a structured narrative and tutorial. Using simple cutscenes across several different scenarios, the game slowly breaks down all of its confusing menus and options into something that becomes more familiar. It even has options to quick-build rooms like cells, kitchens, dining halls, and so on. Still, after more than 235 hours with the title, it felt like there was more to learn in
.
is a deep offering of gameplay elements, interconnected systems, and emergent storytelling, but if all this sounds like more work than fun, you're probably right; this game just isn't for you. However if you're a fan of simulations,
is one of the best there is.

When developing a prequel, make sure the game doesn't take place before the QA team has tested it.  The developers of Batman: AO apparently had one goal: If it isn't broken, fiddle with it until it is.  They took Batman: AC, and managed to break every single aspect of the game in some way or another.  The bugs are innumerable and the developers publicly stated that they would not be fixing any so they would have more time to work on the DLC.  Seriously?
Where to start...Batman occasionally glitches out while gliding in the air like he's bouncing off a platform and actually gains elevation while doing so.  I've gotten stuck on ledges, in objects, and been teleported to my destination when stuck while grappling.  Enemies will sometimes teleport to their fallen companions after being alerted in stealth rooms.  The graphics somehow received a significant downgrade despite including additional eye candy that AC doesn't have along with facial animations from 15 years ago.  It also includes new performance problems that cause the game to stutter badly when flying around the city and in certain rooms indoors.  Side quests regularly break with fights getting stalled or being unable to continue mission steps in the city.  Combat timing feels off with counters being harder to pull off than they should be, and a couple times I had enemies attack me from so far away that even though I had a counter indicator, Batman would ready a gadget rather than countering.  This is made worse by the game wildly varying the timescale during combat.  I've read about some major progression-blocking bugs as well but luckily I never ran into any.
Then come the design problems.  The map has no mouse support and the keyboard moves the cursor in very large increments making it very difficult to select specific locations (I know this won't affect many players but it's inexcusable for the map to be that hard to use with kb/m.)  The game has a lengthy tutorial laboriously explaining the basics but afterwards assumes you have already played the previous games and does not explain anything until after you've failed the first time.  The game includes way too many cutscenes and at several points in the game will drop you back into the game only to have you press one button before starting another cutscene.  Most of the bossfights are long and tedious and a few rather frustrating - none feel well-designed.  During one fight, after one of the frequent in-game cutscenes the boss recovered and hit me before the game gave me control back.  Riddler has been copy-pasted into the game as Enigma except with less personality and extremely simplistic puzzles.  The game includes less interesting characters overall and half the story feels like a rehash of AC.  The new challenge system is strictly linear and will only let you attempt one at a time and most can only be completed in story missions which makes it extremely difficult to complete in one playthrough.  Many ledges are ungrappleable for no reason other than to artificially make it more difficult to reach that location.  Oh, and it seems Batman hasn't learned how to punch through plywood yet despite having more gear than AC and acting like The Hulk the whole game.
The only good thing I found in the game is that you unlock certain gadgets and abilities through side missions, rather than all through the story.  The new martial arts master enemies are pretty interesting as well, though they can make fights a bit unpredictable due to the variable way they react to attacks and counters.
So in summary, they took AC, made every part of the game worse, added a big pile of bugs, and released AO.  Play AA and AC instead or wait for AK.  Save your sanity, I already lost mine.

One of my favourite games, as of today.  It took me about 40 hours to finish and I definitely haven't done nor seen it all!
This prequel to the Arkham series is very well done, in my opinion at least. It does a lot of explaining,it is a visit to the past after you've already seen the present and adds to the overall story of this particular Batman universe. For people like me, who are new to the Batman franchise, it's a great experience. First, in the two games that came out before Origins we see Batman as a hero, known, respected by many, despised by...well, many too I suppose. Now we get to see it wasn't always so.
The story itself was, for me, more absorbing than that of Arkham city. The plot wasn't as comlicated, which does not mean it wasn't rich or interesting. On the contrary, it was both those things. The storytelling was, for me, about as good as Arkham Asylum's, if not better in places. There were some tear jerking moments there and I appreciated those greatly.
The characters were many. We finally got to see Batman's relationship with Gordon as it was before they had formed their "allience". We get to see the beginnings of Enigma, Joker and Harley. Many other characters are presented, some introduced in the Arkham series for the first time. Most of them get decent boss battles, some of them are, however, underused. Which is a pity, but overall it doesn't harm the plot or the gameplay all that much.
The voice acting is spot on in my eyes. Although for the first time we get to hear different voice actors than the ones we are used to from other Arkham games, they all give the characters personalities and life. There's nothing lacking there at all. (Apart from the voice file, which were welcome, even though they weren't as insanity-filled as in the other games, therefore less interesting.)
The graphics of the games are somewhat different than in the previous games. The colours are more dark, gloomy maybe. And it fits the atmosphere very well. The details are fine and sharp.
The map is bigger than before, although not entirely new. Many of the districts were introduced back in Arkham City and it's all that much better because of this. You feel like you've come home once more. You know the city, although it doesn't quite know you yet. Seeing places and buildings you've visited before feels nice, almost nostalgic. That's the part I enjoyed the most - the atmosphere of the city you know so well.
The music is fitting, if not ever-present. It's the opposite of intrusive - it creates the rush necessary - in the Predator encounters, in all the right ways and the right moments throughout the story, in the cutscenes.
As for the gameplay itself, it was very diverse. The main story line was great in the means of battle. Taking down all the assassins, although optional, was a must for me. The boss battles felt all very different, no two were the same. Some required stratedy, others skill. The Predator encounters were an absolute treat. Somehow, when you know you're being "judged" by the games, it drives you forward, you seek success. Anything less than the perfect store isn't acceptable, most of the time anyways. That's a new aspect altogether, leveling up according to your performance, not because the story has progressed. If you perform really well, you're rewarded. You really feel like The Batman this time around. That's the upside of it. For me, though, there was a downside as well. The challenges were present as usual, but they were divided into categories and could only be completed in order. So it doesn't matter how many times you've completed a certain challenge, you'll have to do it again once you reach it. Doing it out of order just doesn't count and that can be infuriating sometimes. Besides some minor bugs in the combat, though, the gameplay feels smooth, familiar-yet-new. The gadgets are the same, yet different. It shows that need for further developement in Batman's equiement, which is what we see in the "later" games (the ones that came before, of course).
Most wanted is a fun part, too. There are several side mission which require Batman's attention and they're, generally, well presented. Enigma's part is easily a fan-favourite, at least for me. Besides Most wanted, there are Investigation missions as well, which are fun, if somewhat odd - B-man's a real genius with huge resources when it comes to crime solving.
Overall, the game is my favourite in the series, even if Asylum will always be the first and the best remembered. Origins provides the player with a rich plot, stories you didn't know you wanted to hear, the beginnings of well-known heroes and villains, smooth and polished gameplay, huge map, nostalgia and a feeling of being The Batman. Even if it wasn't perfect, it exceeded my expectations greatly.

Very useful for those out there who often plays FPS games competitively. Aim Hero currently supports Overwatch, Paladins, and CS:GO. I train myself with Aim Hero if I'm bored and before every CS:GO session for about 5 to 30 minutes and my aim has improved significantly. Ace? done that several times in a few past days. Flick Headshots? done that 3 times in a single round on the last session I played.
Sure some fellas out there said that the classic and reflex training mode is available on custom maps in CS:GO community workshop. But the thing is Aim Hero also provide other modes that haven't been available on the workshop. While I should admit that classic and reflex training in Aim Hero lacks customizations (also in other modes), but I don't think that would be a dealbreaker for me.
Also, the mechanics and hit register is far more smoother than in CS:GO. I don't know if this is a negative thing for Aim Hero or not, since this would mean that Aim Hero doesn't reflect CS:GO's mechanics and hit registers perfectly (lmao).
Including CS:GO's weapon (AK, M4, SMGs) recoil characteristics and its recoil training would make Aim Hero the perfect aim training simulator. Including pre-fire training on several popular maps such as Dust II, Inferno, Cache, or Mirage would also be nice.

Nutshell: 10/10 - Excellent tool to improve your aim in ANY first-person shooter, based off my testing.
Setup - 10/10 - It's actually really simple, in the settings, they have currently got 3 presets for sensitivity, CS:GO, Overwatch, and Paladins, although you can fine-tune some of these things to whatever game you wish to improve on, such as sensitivity.
Gameplay - N/A - Let's be honest, you're not playing this game for fun, you're playing this so you have more fun in OTHER first-person-shooter games by getting better at those other games, such as Overwatch.
Does it Work? - Yes, it does, and it works very well, and is completely foolproof. I've been practicing using Aim Hero for about 2 months now, and actually, if you want to see my progress, watch some of my older gameplay videos of games like Overwatch, Team Fortress 2, CS:GO, etc (IkusaTakuma) then watch my newer ones, it's a huge difference. In games like Overwatch, in only about 10 days, doing Aim Hero only for 10 minutes before playing FPS games, I went from being a Symmetra main in Overwatch to frequently getting gold elims as aim-dependent heroes like Tracer and McCree. In CS:GO I went from occasionally being kicked for being a noob to frequently being in the top 3 on my team.
Things I'd Want to See - not much, I'd love to see more presets for other FPS games like Battlefield and Call of Duty be added, but other than that, please keep Aim Hero the way it is, it's perfect for training as-is.

DmC: Devil May Cry is shameless. It takes a once great character action franchise and dumbs it down for the lowest common denominator. Not only is DmC willing to destroy the foundations that had brought the series the recognition that it had, but it's willing to insult its old fanbase over and over again.
DmC's story and writing are laughably bad, almost as if a prepubescent boy had written it while reading Playboy magazines. The game can never decide whether it was to be taken seriously or not, and the shifts of tone are always jarring.
Combat has been dumbed down significantly. No longer are you required to know your enemies and manage the way you maneuver your character; instead, the game very "kindly" maps all of your directionally sensitive inputs to seperate buttons. Instead of having to push the analog stick (on a controller) in the opposite direction of an enemy to send him to the skies, all you have to do is push the B button. Not only that, but almost all of Dante's moves can be dodge cancelled, which means you no longer have to think about whether a certain combo or move is going to land you in trouble at th wrong time. Just keep mashing the Y button until you win, and if you get into trouble, just keep mashing Y (because then you might parry them with the MASSIVE parry window you have), or just hit LB to simply dodge out of the way.
The music is garbage. It's dubsteppy nonsense mixed with guitar playing that is akin to that of a mouse climbing up and down a fretboard while a man slaps some strings. Nothing is memorable about the game's soundtrack.
Probably the only good thing about the game is its visual style and graphics. The colors really pop and the environments are pretty creative, even if the level design is lazy. They might've just taken a few islands and strung them together to make the world feel big, but at least it looks pretty while you're running around. The character models don't share the same positive light, however. Everyone looks like a big man-baby, and it's ridiculous.
Overall, DmC is a game you should avoid. Please, do not pay for this game. Borrow it or share it from a friend, if you REALLY have to.

Mad Max is surprisingly good. Recommend on sale, would be fine at full price. It was fun to pick up and play during the winter sale. Drive, punch, shoot, loot, build a murdermobile. Beyond that, it's tough to pin down. Keep in mind this is a $20 game shamelessly applying the Ubisoft/WB open world format. It's not Fallout 4, Witcher 3, or Chess.
Pros:
++ Improving your car! The Magnus Opus! Just about every upgrade category is meaningful.
++ Vehicle combat. The vehicle stuff is great. I loved Rock 'N' Roll racing as a kid, and appreciate new and creative action/tactical situations in games. Ramming down barriers, tearing drivers out in-motion with your harpoon, annihilating armored convoys with a shotgun blast to their fuel tanks.. It's good fun!
+ Ground combat. It's again like the AC and Arkham systems, but honestly less gamey. Batman can string together lightning fast counters and ridiculous 40+ hit combos with impunity, surrounded by an army. It's laughable. Max is not quite as ridiculous. Not every counter and heavy hit applies an invincibility animation. If you just mash attack, someone will slash or grab you for damage and break your combo. You can use the shotgun in melee, it's powerful but the ammo restriction keeps it somewhat in check. A large group including shield guys can take some focus. Side note: 100% make sure to impale some poor shmuck with an explosive javelin at least once.
+ Great setting. Cruising the wasteland in your upgradeable battle car is a ton of fun. Combined with great fast travel, this is a welcome improvement on the open world formula. Exploring and progressing are fun and usually efficient, not a chore of walking or climbing to the next goal. The endless expanse of sand is somehow a more interesting place than some other recent game worlds. The hot air balloons instead of climbing towers are another nice alteration.
+ No inventory system, just health, water, and ammo. (Vehicles have fuel, but it's rarely a concern unless you use flamethrowers.) There is only one currency, scrap. Good. Scrounging the wasteland for 'adhesive' is a joke IMO.
+ Surprising variety in locations and missions. Steal vehicles, kill people, win Death Race, save people, aquire a V8 engine.. occasional climbing puzzles and spooky underground explorations
+ Colorful characters
+ Very optional side stuff, including good side missions, races, and taking over camps
+ Burning rubber, Blood, and Explosions
Cons:
-- Many of the features and most optional content/locations add very little to the game - storms, insignias, several location types. Some specifics follow, like certain aspects of srongholds.
- Repetitive, easy boss fights. There are basically 2 boss types, and they're very similar. You either dodge then wail on them, or counter then wail. The Big Bad even mostly follow this. It's unfortunate. This is one reason I stopped doing the camps. Thankfully you can mix in the shotgun or melee weapons, and they're generally short fights.
- Bad ending. No spoilers, but it's bad, and it may be immersion breaking for some if you intend to continue playing after completing the main storyline.
- It's too easy. I usually play games on normal, or about about difficulty level 3.5 out of 5. You may want to look up what actually changes playing on hard, and consider just starting there.
- I don't get the point of the 'scavenging locations' without project parts. There are a dozen better ways to make scrap and refuel.
- Collecting alternate vehicle types feels tacked on and underwhelming. They don't give you parts. You can't fast travel with them. A couple times I drove something back, only to find out it wasn't even collectible. I abandoned this feature. You might enjoy tooling around in a mine layer, or using something super fast like the twelve-cylinder in a race. I preferred just building my Magnus Opus, and enjoying the odd story bit in something else.
Mixed:
. You don't nearly have to fully upgrade Max or the car to finish the game. That's the main source of progression, and fun, so this was a weird sort of let down. It goes with the ease and short length of the main story.
. Side stuff like camps and death runs (races) are almost entirely optional except for a couple mission requirements. I started off thinking I'd do most of the camps for fun and passive income, but it's just not worthwhile unless you're a completionist. The only 'district' I completed was a waste of time, and I never brought a main region's threat to 0. I don't think I even brought any down to 1.
. Sadly, this includes the races. The main story drving events are fantastic, particularly the Death Race scenario. Every side driving event ('death run') seems to just be a forgettable A to B time trial against slow idiots. I quickly stopped doing them.
. Because of all this, fully upgrading the car may be fun for you, or a grindy chore. Thankfully, it's optional after a point.
. Similarly, you can mostly ignore the strongholds. They house main characters, but the middle two are hardly consequential. I got all the perks at one, to refill ammo, health etc. I have no idea why you would bother repeating this several more times. You can just fast travel to your chosen one and refill instantly, almost anytime. Every stronghold also has a stupid 'dump a ton of scrap here' random 'upgrade'. I looked it up. They cost a ton, and do nothing meaningful or interesting. Beyond doing what he must to survive and improve the car, the whole idea of community and base building is at odds with the Max' motivations anyway. It doesn't really fit, thematically. He wants out of Dodge (and into a murder machine).
. Storms. Scary, then exciting, then minor annoyance.

It is pretty much unheard of for a movie that is now a game to actually be any good.  Transformers did a pretty good job, and that was literally it.  Until now....
Mad Max is visually appealing and the gameplay in itself is fantastic.  The game really shines when it comes to driving and vehicular combat, and this is the best part of the game for sure. It is also a very key aspect of the game. Throw in a ton of different upgrades and weapons for both Max and his vehicle, and you have a lot of options for ending the wastelanders trying to kill you at every turn. As for the hand to hand combat, some are comparing it to the Batman games, but it is nothing like it. The combat is rather simplistic, parry, dodge, attack, charge strike, etc. But the effects when you are fighting enemies is quite fun.  For instance, attack someone against a wall or a car, and Max will pin them to it while visciously beating them down.  Don't like the way that Warboy spoke to you, finish him off with a brutal shiv to the brain stem. And yes, the violent attacks are delivered quite brutally.  It is also fun to launch a quick strike from your shotgun, or aim, if you prefer.  I really enjoy how the shotgun is pretty useless at any real range. Which is exactly how it should be.
The games world is pretty big, and you really do feel like you are driving through the wasteland. The need for fuel is there, but not oppresive to where it deters from your gameplay and enjoyment. Same with health. It will not just regenerate.  Instead you need to find food or water, and of course none of these things are just lying around.
There are also a lot of different things to do. And while it could be seen as busy work, the side quests and random things to do aren't random. They help you progress through areas more easily, and are always fun to engage in.  For example, using the harpoon to kill snipers in their towers, or blowing up the scarecrows. It's always fun and entertaining to engage in.
The only bad thing I have to say about this game is that the button prompts are not exactly accurate.  For example, it will tell you to press the same button that you parry with when it is time to finish an enemy off with a shiv strike, but that does not work. The actual key is your use key.  For example, the Y button on my controller is for parrying blows. It should work for a shiv strike, but in actuality it is a completely different button. Kind of annoying, and seems a simple thing that should not occur, but it does. You might also run in to this during the usage of vehicle weapons, like the harpoon. It is annoying because you cannot remove the pop ups and the button you need to press is in fact different from what the game is telling you. So you might just end up pressing the wrong button many times thanks to the pop ups that just wont go away.

This game is fun and a great starting point if you want to get into SCS's Truck sim games as its quite smaller than ETS2 and has a few less features to worry about, this game is very similar to ETS2 with a few differences, for example in ETS2 you have to save up or take a loan to get your first truck but in this one you are made to buy your very first truck straight away and the way you take jobs is set differently too.
I have this game on my Tablet PC running a 1.66ghz atom processor and it runs smoothly with no visible issues, therefore it would be the better game to grab if you are wanting something with very low specifications for journeys on public transport or if you are a passenger on a road trip, there are a few flaws with the game but nothing thats too game breaking, if you have played ETS2 or even Scania truck driver simulator this game will feel outdated and primitive, however if you are looking to get into the series you cant go wrong with getting this game as part of the SCS deluxe package as you will get alot more value for your money.
all in all this game has aged very well and even to this days standards looks like a very well made indie game however you will feel dissapointed if you come from one of the newer games in the series, i will not go as far as to label this game as a high quality game but it is for the most part a decent playable game that can keep you going for endless ammounts of playing as you strive to work for bigger jobs or better trucks.
If you are looking for a highly detailed yet smoothly running truck simulator you cannot go wrong with this title, however if you want a more up to date feel with even better graphics, go for ETS2. if you cannot decide go for the deluxe bundle as you will get 5 titles and a whole bunch of DLC for ETS2.

is a top-down simulation game like the ages-old Tycoon games on PC. You're tasked with overseeing all aspects of prison management. The developer,
, truly has thought of everything in this regard, too. You build the prison from the ground up, lay water pipes and electrical wiring, hire staff like guards, doctors, and therapists, install surveillance and emergency countermeasures, and if you eventually have the prison running as it should, then you have to keep it that way.
This is done by keeping the population of inmates fed, content, nonviolent, and within the walls and fences of the institution. Because you're also operating a private prison, the endgame is to also make money.
The introduction to the game's many systems can be extremely intimidating at first. Thankfully, this feeling of being overwhelmed is largely undone using the game's Prison Stories mode that doubles as a structured narrative and tutorial. Using simple cutscenes across several different scenarios, the game slowly breaks down all of its confusing menus and options into something that becomes more familiar. It even has options to quick-build rooms like cells, kitchens, dining halls, and so on. Still, after more than 235 hours with the title, it felt like there was more to learn in
.
is a deep offering of gameplay elements, interconnected systems, and emergent storytelling, but if all this sounds like more work than fun, you're probably right; this game just isn't for you. However if you're a fan of simulations,
is one of the best there is.
My personal favorite.
THE GOOD
- Great gameplay
- Emergent story moments and character backgrounds for all inmates
- Building/management freedom
- Great tutorial
- Deals with sociopolitical themes surprisingly well and maturely
- Freedom to run the prisons in many different ways
THE BAD
- Minimal sound design
- Lacks soundtrack

DmC Devil May Cry is a fantastic re-imaging of the popular hack and slash series that follows the part demon, part angel nephilim, Dante. Players will make their way through a series of levels that are split between Limbo and Reality, while fighting demons and other monstrosities along the way. Fans of the series initially bashed the game for the new aesthetic stylings that have changed how Dante looks. But this is of little consequence seeing as how his attitude has also been tweaked. He may well come across as an angsty 20-something year old at first, but as the character grows he quickly becomes a solid Dante in his own right, with a strong moral code and personality. Combat is fast, strong and fluid, you can really feel the impact of the various weapons that you will be bringing to battle; be it sword, scythe or ranged weapons, they all pack enough punch to make the ranking combat system worth engaging in. Fans of the series will see some returning faces and ideals, and for those of you that purchase the DL, "Vergils Downfall" this game could be considered a prequel to Devil May Cry 3. DmC: Devil May Cry is actually a reboot, but some hardcore fans differ on this decision, thus aligning the timeline:
DmC Devil May Cry
Devil May Cry 3
Devil May Cry 1
Devil May Cry 4
Devil May Cry 2
But putting that subject aside, this game is damn near perfect with great add on DLC including the free Bloody Palace Mode, definitely a game for fans of sword play. Just like my original review of the game, Dmc Devil May Cry would be scored 9/10.
But Steam doesn't score that way, so consider it recommended.

Rust is a game of patience and persistence, and you experience that the moment you start the game, and that turns a lot of people off. As of recently, updates have been kiling the game, but I have hope for this wonderful game. This game attracts the player who enjoys sitting down and grinding and having their work pay off (most of the time), but it also attracts cucks, so watch out. I reccomend playing this game with a veteran if you're new, but once you get the ist, I reccomend playing solo, to better understand the game. Overall, I rate this game 7/10.

While Rust is an early access game, the developers and designers are constantly making updates and changes not only to the functionality of the gameplay, but to the graphics and perfomance as well. While the constant updating can be an upside to the EA norm of getting greenlit and then never touching your game again, the updates have also been a headache to those that loved the game at a specific stage of development and would rather it not change.
It's a fun game with a really fun premise of survival and base building. PvP is constantly being tweaked and PvE is having its ups and downs as well. If you get this game, don't settle in for how it is at any given point and expect things to change from week to week each Thursday.
I would recommend this game to anyone that likes PvP survival games with crafting and building elements. I would not recommend this game to anyone wanting a finished game that won't change. Please believe me when I say this game will change. The hings you love may be deprecated while the things you hate may be promoted.

Been playing Rust for about 4 years now. When the game came out it was truly a one of a kind experience, and the market quickly populated with games that emulated certain aspects of Rust. While it could be argued that DayZ was the originator of this genre, I would argue that Rust innovated enough with base building, and brought much more depth to player interaction.
But the question at hand isn't whether Rust is historically relevant in the gaming world. It's whether Rust is a good game or not. While I might claim that this game sucks when I'm angry, it also has brought me a lot of joy. I've met some people in the game that I've gone on to play other games with, too. The daily life of Rust can be sometimes frustrating, but thats what's amazing about the game. It lends itself to large amounts of randomness and unpredictabilitly.
Buy Rust. Play it. It's never too late to get started tbh.

The developers have made good on all the crimes they commited in Absolution and brought back the solid Hitman experience previously found in the series.
Massive levels greet you with a broadside of opportunities to finish your contracts, and each (re-)completed contract will help to extend your arsenal and provide even more possibilities to get the job done - adding a great deal of replayability as you not only try to achieve previously hidden ways of assassin-mastery, but also try to improve your score on every playthrough.
While your inventory is sadly not managed similar to "Blood Money" and you don't have the ability to personally modify and upgrade your weapons you still get a whole bunch of intelligence-community grade gadgets and weapons - which at times strongly remind of James Bond movies, thereby keeping your inventory a relevant and interessting place.
The map-intel has moved from the map to the actual HUD through the use of Absolution's "Instinct". While in this release the use of instinct doesn't deplete anything it has also been weakend down to the point where it only serves as a tool to identify PoIs, and observe NPC routines.
It can therefore not be used to take out many enemies rapidly, to predict the pathing of NPCs, or to escape detection.
Speaking of the latter, no longer will every policeman, every chef, every guard know the other persons in his profession by sight - Detection has been changed to make actual sense, and only certain boss-ish characters will now be able to discover 47's "true" identity.
Now should there come a time when you are no longer interessted in the actual mission objectives themselves, you have these options to pick from:
- play user-created contracts (in this release they actually make sense!)
- play escalation contracts (to get more level points as well)
- create a contract yourself
- play one of the elusive contracts
I can but give the warmest recommandation for this title to any Hitman (even stealth game) enthusiast, they have put an enormous amount of work into this and every Episode is worth its price at full.

Aside from maybe Stardew Valley, the most fun I've had with any release in 2016. It feels like a true sequel to blood money, and is the rare example of a stealth game where you don't spend 90% of the time crouching behind walls and sneaking behind people's backs (except for silent assassin/suit only runs, which are exactly what I just described)
The way the levels are laid out encourages exploration, creativity, and replayability. Learning the clockwork of a level and its inhabitants, and finding the best time and way to strike, then going back and perfecting it and tackling it from different angles makes for great gameplay. It is also a very funny game, with many comedic moments both scripted ("Dad? Please call me, it happened again") and unscripted.
The episodic format doesn't really bother me, but then again I purchased it once all the episodes were already out, so that didn't really bother me. That said, the format lends itself better than expected for the kind of game it is, especially considering how light on story it is. The game is constantly updated with new content, including escalations, elusive targets, featured/custom contracts, and the recent addition of a professional difficulty.
There are three big negatives I would mention, the only real three complaints I have
--Always online DRM, game must be played online otherwise content is strictly limited
--The same 4-5 voice actors doing all the background characters in the game. Less voice acting variety than Skyrim
--Time locked elusive missions that punish anyone waiting for a sale or too busy to play a given week. Content that is gone forever if not played at a specific time
NOTE: You'll have a much better time if you turn off all the handholding tools like instinct and opportunity modes. Maybe even turn off the minimap
Overall 9/10. If blending into crowds, disguising yourself as any number of things from an intern to a vampire magician, and setting up overly elaborate Rube Goldbergian deathtraps for the global elite sounds like it appeals to you, give the first chapter a try and either give up or go from there based on how you like it

Over many years ( I was six when my dad brought Pong home ) there have been a number of games that led to hours of binge playing. From Missle Command on Atari 2600 to Ninja Gaiden on Nintendo to Sonic on Genesis to Final Fantasy 7 and Final Fantasy Tactics on Playstation to Morrowind on the Xbox and then into a slew of PC games far too long to list.
Without a doubt the Arkham series fits into this category. Every game, so far, has stolen far more hours of my life away than I would care to contemplate. I mean what could be better than being Batman? Especially when Harley Quinn is always around to provide a bit of eye candy!

This review won't be a normal one. I just want to get some different stuff off my chest:
I love this series, but after having played all three of them back to back now, I have to question just how much of it was playing the story, and how much was simply screwing around trying to get all the riddler thingies.
...and once you're done, you can maybe get around 50% game completion, because then there's all the challenges and game modes and stuff. Do you play Batman, or do you play a person with obessive compulsive disorder?
...because only a mentally ill player would get more than 50% game completion. No game is so good that you would think that making an online account and playing online with 100 other Batmen, and viewing all the concept art, and getting all the trophies, would be a good idea.
...and I also have to question Batman's very persona: He's some kind of crossing between a super cop, and a bloodthirsty monster. He can be all tough against crime, and even beat up defenseless people for fun, but he stops short of killing them, and not even he knows why. "It's not the way I do things." he repeats, as the villains mock him for it throughout the game. "It's not the way." I'm fine with him not killing people, but he clearly hasn't thought things through philosophically.
It's as if Batman is in love with violence, but prides himself on never killing his victims, trying to cover up for his bloodlust by claiming to fight crime. This becomes even more bizarre considering the amount of damage this hulking dude deals out. Realistically, maybe 25% of his victims would die from complications within days or even hours. Dislocating or breaking wrists and ankles, is a move in this game, sometimes on dudes who are begging for mercy.
...but again: Don't bother with collecting all the millions of riddler thingies, because it won't be worth it. I was severely disappointed when I saw what my reward was. The reward in Arkham City was much better,
Either the combat is slower or I'm just bothered by the fact that this isn't the first game.

Regardless of the vitriolic hatred aimed at this game by its rabid "fanboi" populace, this is possibly the most solid entry in the entire DMC series.  With a stronger focus on quality storytelling than prior titles, DmC: Devil May Cry provides a much more coherent, "all growed up" retelling of Dante's origin.  Accompanying this excellent narrative is an incredibly solid artistic style.  The environments, special effects and monster design are all quite fresh.  Creatures you encounter are instantly recognizable; there will be no confusing one demon for another.  The soundtrack also remains superb, as one would expect from this series.  Granted, it's a slightly different style of soundtrack, featuring more electronica (of the industrial variety) and less heavy metal-inspired tracks.
Now for the critiques...
DmC features an "angel" and "demon" weapon system.  At first blush, this seems like a perfectly reasonable tweak/addition to the game.  First impressions would lead you to believe that it livens up combos and adds more variety to the game.  This is, however, only half true.  The angel/demon weapon system can, in some cases, leave you more limited in your combo choices.  When a designated angel/demon enemy type is struck by anything other than a matching weapon, the weapon bounces off harmlessly, (which also leaves Dante open and vulnerable for a moment) ending any combo chain you may be in the middle of.
Throw just one of these enemies into a mix of other types, and you are forced to either A.) Remove that enemy from the group with a pull (which, granted, the game gives you the tools for) or B.) Kill the whole group with a matching weapon type.
Over all, this isn't a huge deal, and you won't often be bothered by it.  There are criticisms to be made about this system, however, so you might find yourself occasionally irritated by the situations you're put into.
The Vergil's Downfall DLC is also fairly disappointing.  Vergil's combo list is, generally speaking, much smaller and more sparsely populated with techniques than his brother Dante's.  This leaves Vergil's fights feeling a bit stale and repetitive until every option for his combat is unlocked (and even then, it's less in-depth than Dante's is).
The cutscenes of Vergil's downfall also features a completely different visual style.  In Vergil's Downfall, the cutscenes are comprised of minimalistic animations, as opposed to the motion-captured CGI of the main game.  While not necessarily inferior, it can be visually jarring when one goes from the main game straight into the DLC.
Anyway, that about wraps it up.  This is a solid game, with little to actually complain about once the nostalgia glasses come off.  Fans of the original DMC (myself included) and its subsequent sequels should feel right at home here, assuming they are capable of being objective and unbiased.

Euro Truck Simulator is a 2008 truck simulation game created by SCS Software, using OpenGL, set in Europe. The player can drive across a depiction of Europe, visiting its cities, picking up a variety of cargos, and delivering them. Over 300,000 copies of the game have been sold in Europe. Its followup, Euro Truck Simulator 2, was released in 2012.
Players choose their starting country, from Austria, Belgium, Czech Republic, France, Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Spain, Switzerland and the United Kingdom (V1.2 & V1.3 only). Initially players only have access to their starting country, except if it contains less than three cities. In this case one or more adjacent countries will be accessible as well. For example, starting the game in Italy or Switzerland, you get connection to the other for free. Then, players choose their first truck with a budget of €100,000.After this, players can start taking jobs from various fictitious companies and delivering cargo to various cities in their starting country to earn money. This money can then be spent on a new truck, upgrading the current truck, expanding the business to other countries and obtaining a license to drive flammables and chemicals.

So, yeah. Mad Max. I got completely hooked (a few years late considering the major wave has passed a long time ago) a year ago, after seeing the newest movie (sue me for loving it). I completely drained the internet ou tof anything related to Mad Max - including this game.
I've played driving and racing games ever since I turned 10 years old, so for almost 20 years now. And I still don't like using WASD for driving. It's NOT horrible, though. Some of the controls are sticky and tricky, behind the wheel and on foot. Why on earth would you need to keep pushing a button down to activate an item? Whoever thought of that must've not played a single game in their life. Because that is stupid. Just plain stupid, and slow. SLOW. IN MAD MAX. At least the game is mostly bug-free, doesn't freeze and runs smoothly. It has a lot of cool little features, almost like minigames, like fueling up the hot air balloons (or their generators), picking for loot, destroying insignia, collecting car types and history relics, not forgetting the racing.
Improving Max's attributes is kinda fun and rewarding. Easy enough, too.
I did hate the autosave at first, because there is no option to save manually (sometimes forcing an autosave is possible, but doesn't always work?), but actually the autosave is intelligent enough, thus bearable.
Sometimes the story does seem like it was written by a gore-loving teen, especially when it comes to the character descriptions and history relics (I mean, you can't make Max unemphatetic and callous while he is mad, sad and decisive at the same time?!), but most of them are good. I don't care so much for the way they tried, or rather, forced Max's voice to sound like a sleazy halfwit trying too hard to be cool and commancing people. Every other character's voice actor carries themselves pretty damn great.
If you got hooked on the new Mad Max movie, you'll enjoy the game, because addictions like Mad Max need to be fed with whatever you can lay your hands on. The game does deliver, most of the time. One MAJOR miss is the lack of strong female characters. We only get Pink Eye, who is a boringly common image of a warrior woman. She's old, wounded, raises kids - you know, because she's a woman - and leads in a just, strong way. You never see male characters raising kids in these stories. Except for, you know, IMMORTAN ♥♥♥♥ING JOE. Where did that idea go?! This is exactly what George Miller was trying to prove differently, that a female character is not just an old lioness. A female character can be badass, and a badass without being a♥♥♥♥♥♥ And a male character can be a♥♥♥♥♥♥*cough* SLIT *cough* without being a♥♥♥♥♥♥at all. In MM:FR movie we had plenty of different kinds of strong women from the heavenly Angharad to the tender Capable and the vicious Valkyrie. Oh and then there was Furiosa. I mean what the♥♥♥♥♥♥ That woman was one hell of a fighter and never made her gender a thing. I wanted to see warriors like that in this game, too - men, women, whatever. Heck, make more female villains as well. Make ONE! MM:FR made women feel equal to men in strength and leadership style as well as skillset. I miss that in this game. A lot. (Disclaimer: I'm a non-feminist white bisexual male, just because there's gotta be someone out there thinking I'm making this a girl power thing. I'm making this a Mad Max Fury Road KICKASS WARRIORS OF ALL GENDERS FROM EVERY ANGLE AND CONSTANT FEELING OF AROUSAL -kind of thing.)
The cars you can create for yourself are pretty magnificen. I mean, I wanna rent a garage and start on building that Buzzard wheeler with rusty spikes and questionably shiny colour choices (mostly chrome).
The lore is interestingly tied to the newest movie, but it's also interesting and takes liberties and introduces new material.
To a serious addict like myself, the camera feature is a ♥♥♥♥ing genious addition. The game isn't luxuriously beautiful, but it's beautiful enough to boost your imagination when you take pictures of those really cool war boy establishments. Tents, caves, ship wrecks and aircraft bodies. THEY ARE SO FRIGGIN' COOL AND I WANT TO LIVE IN THEM.
I miss Cinnamon Roll & Lizard King & Red, though. (Nux, Slit, and Capable.) Very, very, very much. I was hoping against hope to see them again.
(Jeet does a grand job in trying to cover for all three of them though.)
tl;dr
All in all, yeah... Buy it for the game or buy it for the movie, it's a nice way to pass some time. As a game, 8/10 "it works and it doesn't hurt your eyes", as a story, maybe 7/10 "interesting enough but nothing super special", as a Mad Max addict, 9/10 "I love everything but I miss the emotional arousal of MM:FR experience".

Oh boy, where to start...
Let's make a few points clear first.
-I got this game pretty recently, didn't focus much on it, as I'm still getting used to it.
-I bought this game durring Summer Sales, as the price of almost 20 Euros is a bit too much in my opinion.
------------GOOD THINGS ABOUT THE GAME-------------
1) I love driving games ok? I always pretty much wanted to be on a server and have a realistic driving scene, which in games like Gmod is near to impossible.
2) This game has the steering wheel support. I unfortunately use a racing steering controller but it still works good for me and I run my truck smoothly.
3) The graphics in this game are stunning. I, myself, have an average PC, not a gaming one, in fact I have to run the game on medium graphic settings to get at least 60-50 FPS. Max graphic settings are really really worth a try if you got a gaming PC. They look bloody awesome.
4) The DLCs in this game are good looking and each of every DLC has a really lot to add to the game, ranging from cool looking paintjobs to a whole section of europe (Scandinavia or Going East!).
5) How to forget the Multiplayer mode? Multiplayer is practically what makes this game really entretaining. In fact, seeing trucks passing by and making a small horn sound to say hello to you is really satisfying! Multiplayer takes a bit of time to install and get it working [Installer - Installing || Making account || Verifying] But trust me it's worth every millisecond.
6) This game pretty much has the whole europe. And since it would be too big for a game, they reduced the road, not too much, not too less, so it's basically perfect fit. Another reason why I love this game.
7) Radios too! Exactly, IRL radios in game. Lovely.
8) Realistic weather is looking awesome! I love the rain in the game, also every period of the day and night is perfect... One thing pretty awesome too is the options in the game. They pretty much let you set the difficulty (From rain chance to Fuel consumption to even money penalities from fines).
there are sooo many things I could say about this game, but I don't want to put too much stuff.
----------------CONS ABOUT THE GAME----------------------
no game is perfect, even tho this one is close to beeing to
1) AI in SP is a bit weird ok? I am pretty sure it happened once or twice to everyone that soem random car or bus would not stop and hit the trailer causing a really high amount of damage (Plus the bill of the car accident, that technically should be paid by the guy who hit you).
2) Earning money in this game is a tough challenge. You need to make a hell lot of travels to get your own truck and company, then to hire another guy... This game is worth the time, even though many players use CheatEngine to get themselves XP. It's their own decision of they want to enjoy the ENTIRE game, or if they want to enjoy the game bit by bit. slowly discovering it.
3) Multiplayer is probably one of the only reasons you might play this game for an extended period of time (At least in my opinion), because SP, with nobody around you, in a night time it's yeah... pretty boring. So MP is kinda necessary if you want to spend a lot of time in this game.
4) The game physics can be a bit glitchy sometimes... In the recent versions it happened a few times to get stuck in the ground, and that would instantly make you a 100% damage. and it's pretty annoying if you are making a 0% dmg delivery and at the end you screw up everything.
-------------------PROS OF MULTIPLAYER ((THIS SECTION IS FOR WHO HAS GOT MULTIPLAYER))----------------------
1) Playing with friends. They even made a script that basically, Green dots on the GPS are your friends. while BLU ones are other players.
2) Enjoying your time while making deliveries, laughing off a ridicoulus and hilarious accident between two trucks! And yes it's sometimes pretty hilarious.
3) You can become a pilot of a truck, using your car, which is a MultiPlayer only addon. The SCOUT car is well made and works fine for me. Pretty awesome veichle to be put in a game. (There is a possibility to become Police too! but that is admin only).
4) No collision zones / Voice communication in game / Chat communication / You can even make a MP company where players can actually work there! Awesome...
If you made it till the end, I hope I helped you with this. This game is really good. and it's really recommended in all senses. so get when the next sales (Christmas or Summer) Happen!
Good luck with everything. the road waits for you.

Verdict: Like 47 himself: Always in motion, always changing, always unpredictable. A fat 9.7/10
What you have before you here is an original Hitman title.
The developers have made good on all the crimes they commited in Absolution and brought back the solid Hitman experience previously found in the series.
Massive levels greet you with a broadside of opportunities to finish your contracts, and each (re-)completed contract will help to extend your arsenal and provide even more possibilities to get the job done - adding a great deal of replayability as you not only try to achieve previously hidden ways of assassin-mastery, but also try to improve your score on every playthrough.
While your inventory is sadly not managed similar to "Blood Money" and you don't have the ability to personally modify and upgrade your weapons you still get a whole bunch of intelligence-community grade gadgets and weapons - which at times strongly remind of James Bond movies, thereby keeping your inventory a relevant and interessting place.
The map-intel has moved from the map to the actual HUD through the use of Absolution's "Instinct". While in this release the use of instinct doesn't deplete anything it has also been weakend down to the point where it only serves as a tool to identify PoIs, and observe NPC routines.
It can therefore not be used to take out many enemies rapidly, to predict the pathing of NPCs, or to escape detection.
Speaking of the latter, no longer will every policeman, every chef, every guard know the other persons in his profession by sight - Detection has been changed to make actual sense, and only certain boss-ish characters will now be able to discover 47's "true" identity.
Now should there come a time when you are no longer interessted in the actual mission objectives themselves, you have these options to pick from:
- play user-created contracts (in this release they actually make sense!)
- play escalation contracts (to get more level points as well)
- create a contract yourself
- play one of the elusive contracts
I can but give the warmest recommandation for this title to any Hitman (even stealth game) enthusiast, they have put an enormous amount of work into this and every Episode is worth its price at full.

Well I was expecting BEEP to be a lot worse that it looks like at first glance - yet another 2D platformer.
Still, the controls aren't insultingly clunky, and the artwork, while really low effort, isn't the worst I've seen either.
Should you buy BEEP, then?  No, not really.  It's got fewer flaws than most 2D platformers, but neither is it the king of the genre.
Also, technical problems prevent the game from being run under Windows 10 if you have a high res display and use DPI (required if your PPI is at or near retina level).   Overscan means you can only access 1/4 of the screen with your mousepointer in full screen mode - you have to run it windowed.
So, while not worth buying, it's worth acknowledging the game is polished enough to be tolerable, meaning at least some of the developers on the project could achieve greater things in future.

Aside from maybe Stardew Valley, the most fun I've had with any release in 2016. It feels like a true sequel to blood money, and is the rare example of a stealth game where you don't spend 90% of the time crouching behind walls and sneaking behind people's backs (except for silent assassin/suit only runs, which are exactly what I just described)
The way the levels are laid out encourages exploration, creativity, and replayability. Learning the clockwork of a level and its inhabitants, and finding the best time and way to strike, then going back and perfecting it and tackling it from different angles makes for great gameplay. It is also a very funny game, with many comedic moments both scripted ("Dad? Please call me, it happened again") and unscripted.
The episodic format doesn't really bother me, but then again I purchased it once all the episodes were already out, so that didn't really bother me. That said, the format lends itself better than expected for the kind of game it is, especially considering how light on story it is. The game is constantly updated with new content, including escalations, elusive targets, featured/custom contracts, and the recent addition of a professional difficulty.
There are three big negatives I would mention, the only real three complaints I have
--Always online DRM, game must be played online otherwise content is strictly limited
--The same 4-5 voice actors doing all the background characters in the game. Less voice acting variety than Skyrim
--Time locked elusive missions that punish anyone waiting for a sale or too busy to play a given week. Content that is gone forever if not played at a specific time
NOTE: You'll have a much better time if you turn off all the handholding tools like instinct and opportunity modes. Maybe even turn off the minimap
Overall 9/10. If blending into crowds, disguising yourself as any number of things from an intern to a vampire magician, and setting up overly elaborate Rube Goldbergian deathtraps for the global elite sounds like it appeals to you, give the first chapter a try and either give up or go from there based on how you like it

Sister Location is very different from the traditional FNaF games where you sit in a office (or bedroom) and defend yourself until 6:00 am. Although some fans of FNaF would prefer the traditional mechanics of previous games, it feels good to get something a bit more innovative and participative crawling through rooms and vents, turning springlocks, and various other tasks that could get you killed. Not only is the gameplay great but the story is there as well. Story hidden in minigames, sounds, voice lines, and easter eggs.
TL;DR

I was really expecting this game to be great, but it was the exact opposite. When the trailer was first released people were going crazy over this game saying that it would be free-roam and all that, but all we got was garbage.
The game felt really rushed overall. It's probably one of the most unique games in the franchise, being that you're not doing the same thing every night, but this could have been way better.
I also wanted to mention that the game tries way too hard to be funny. The jokes, to be honest, are quite stale, whether it be the jokes in the little cartoons you get at the end of each night, or the overused "E X O T I C  B U T T E R S" which wouldn't get the hell off of YouTube for well over a month.
This might also be the hardest game in the franchise. From the second night the difficulty ramps up way too fast, especially in Night 4. The secret ending in Night 5 requires you to do way too much in order to unlock it, and once you finally do manage to it's a massive pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to get past 4:00AM in the secret room.
This game had so much potential, but this is easily the worst game in the franchise, especially considering that long time FNAF fans were expecting free roam, which the Joy of Creation (a Fangame) did much better. I've failed to have much fun with this game, even after well over a year.
