Coffin of Ashes is a beautiful game, the designs and character portraits are nicely detailed and work well to create a good atmosphere. The whole game reminds me a bit of Mad Father (which isn't a bad thing) but it still feels like it's own game. Characters have their own distinct appearances while the ghosts look suitably creepy (especially the teddies, seeing those made me nervous every time I went to a save point afterwards). I do also have to praise the puzzles as I think they're really effective and fun to figure out. One of the best parts of the puzzles is the lack of backtracking, you don't move on from an area until you've done everything you need to and once you're in the next part you just keep moving forward. I love games that do this, as while backtracking can work well in some situations it can also very frustrating. Furthermore everything is there to further the story even if it's just in little character moments, in fact the rest area allows you to learn more details if you want to. Some of the chase sequences got frustrating but it doesn't take too much trial an error to get them right. The only technical issue I have with the game is that some of the translations are a little off, not enough to ruin the experience but they are noticeable at times.
The story however is... alright, it was engaging enough that I wanted to know what would happen next but nothing groundbreaking or shocking really occurred. I am a little annoyed that one of the best twists in the plot was revealed rather hastily at the end through exposition to the player rather than being something the characters themselves figured out, it feels like a wasted opportunity for something that was not only interesting but helped make sense of other things in the plot to just be tacked on at the end. But there wasn't anything wrong with the story as a whole. I liked the characters well enough, though the main character Delilah felt a little bland; her character portraits made me think that she was going to be one of those characters that always seem emotionless while secretly being quite deep, but if that was the intention it didn't really come across in the dialogue. The others are alright, Ian and Lilin were good companions but my favourite person overall was definitely the Deacon, as he's the only one of the side characters who really showed some personality in his conversation. Like the story the characters aren't bad, they just aren't anything to write home about.
Overall if you do like RPGMaker horror-adventure games such as Mad Father, I do think this is worth checking out as the presentation is great and the puzzles are fantastic. While the story wasn't anything amazing it was still good, and for the price it is there isn't anything to complain about.
Oh, and that 'Close Encounters' achievement? That can get stuck in an eternal loop trying to leave a haunted mansion because getting that was an absolute pain!

Freshman Year Review – Raymond KT
Summary: Freshman Year is a vignette game about an ordinary night in the life a college freshman named Nina. Nina's best friend Jenna invites her to meet up at a local bar with some classmates. Jenna is sort of flaky though, so Nina has to navigate the party by herself. You play as Nina, texting with her friend Jenna as you mingle, dance, drink and wait.
Nina Freeman’s short, illustrated interactive fiction game Freshman Year made me feel sick. It did this because it shows how a young woman being in a public place can be interpreted as sexual availability by a man who shows no interest in asking what she wants, and instead believes he can just take what he wants.
Because I am a man I do not experience those same risks; I am, largely speaking, free to socialise and dance and drink without becoming a target for someone else’s desires, and without great risk that they will act on them without my permission. I felt sick because I realised that I’ve often preoccupied myself with the miseries of knock-backs or shyness, but I’ve never once thought how terrifying it can be to be on the other side. To be seen as public property simply because one is in public.
Freshman Year is light and shade. It starts with the freedom and vibrancy of a youth with minimal responsibilities, and collapses into the menace of more physically powerful figures and the terrifying vulnerability which results.
If you or someone you care about has ever experienced sexual abuse or harassment, please be warned that Freshman Year discusses these topics. It is not heavy-handed about it it, not does it contain NSFW imagery; it achieves all it needs to with short sentences, simple art and deeply disquieting sound effects, and it is confident enough in what it means to convey that it leaves the player to draw some of their own conclusions.

I loved Absolution. This plays a lot like Absolution BUT is a little harder. It is still very playable but you really must do your homework before just blasting people in the face. That said...
It was WAY too short. It took me 2 hours (a good player would have it done in 1 hour) to complete the training mission and the ONE mission you get for $14.99. Luckily my friend got it for me on sale (ty) but even still.
I can not see buying the rest until maybe the entire package is around $30. I had fun I really did. This was not even close to enough content to justify the cost.
If this is what I have to go on, expecting maybe 1-3 hours of gameplay per mission, then for a total of $60 you might get 15-20 of game time if you are just playing the missions, which is all I primarily do. I try to aim for a avg of $ 2-3/ hr on a game. Some shoot for $5/hr. Your milage may vary.
The only way this is even worth the cost is for those die hard completionists that will play the mission 17 times to unlock the challenges.
I do NOT recommend buying this solely on the basis that there does not appear to be enough content for the asking price.
Graphics- 4/5 - running my 980 with a 4.4 ghz OC 8320, I ran into some bottleneck somewhere. Probably CPU. I was able to get 60fps in 1080p MOST of the time. It looks pretty good and runs well but it is very taxing and hard to maintain 60 when things pop off or a lot is happening. I had to turn a lot of the settings down below high to avg 55 in game. The cutscenes were massively improved in quality from Absolution. The lighting effects were not to my liking and some of the textures just seemed very dull. The character models were very good.
Sound- 4/5 - Not much to say here. Nothing special. Nothing wrong with it. Dialog sounded good, sound effects were good. A slight improvement in some areas from the last game.
Gameplay- 3/5 I started using mouse and keyboard but found xbox 360 controller to be much easier. There was a few issues with sticking to cover at random and some general jankiness that was uncomfortable at times. I could control my walk speed and direction much easier on the controller than the m/kb. Otherwise, it takes what I liked about Absolution and added some new challenges. Patience is certainly required. I gave it a 3 because it was not as smooth overall as the last game and felt rushed in some aspects. For the price, I would have expected a lot more to be polished. A lot could be worked out such as janky controls and some of the AI is less than stellar. It is very playable. It took a few steps forward and a few steps back IMO in quality of gameplay.
Overall - 3/5 I am factoring in price, time spent, and quality of product. Think of this as the Madden of stealth games. Its a "new roster", some "new grass" and a "new gameplay mechanic" but that is about it. Also they want more money for less content. I really don't think its worth what they want even if it is AAA.
tl;dr
AAA status should not automatically get you a $60 price tag. You have to deliver something worth that much money, and I just don't believe this is worth it.
UPDATE-
I went ahead and changed from Not recommended to Yes recommended. I bought the remaining episodes on sale. I would say for $30 the bundle is worth it. I still feel that $60 was asking too much for what you actually get. It is fun and I do enjoy playing but I think the "non sale" price tage is too high for the total package.

Review related to the October 2017 update (blueprints 3.0). Current date : October 12th 2017.
Been playing the game on and off since Legacy.
Most of the negative reviews you see that focus on this update don't do the game justice. Earlier updates progressively turned the game into a 24-hour PUBG-like, focused heavily on PvP with advanced weaponry available immediately after a server wipe.
The latest update reintroduced something that had been previously removed from the game : progression. A much requested and needed part of the game which is, as too many people forgot or didn't know, a Survival game, and not a Battle Royale.
The so-called "grind" really only is progression. The grind isn't any more intensive than it was before. It just means that you have to actually use the lower-tier gear while you progress through the game before you can actually access rocket launchers and stuff (although this isn't all exactly true for big clans who aren't that much affected by the update, but that's another topic).
To be perfectly honest, Rust is in a much better stay than it was the past months. It's not perfect (it never was, probably won't ever be), what it needs right now is mainly number tweaking (costs for researching blueprints, craft, etc.).
tl;dr : Rust is slowly going back to what it originally was. Lots of recent players are showing discontent because they discovered Rust in a different state, and they liked it better that way.

I actually recommend playing a small bit with unlimited funds with the challanges, gangs, temperature etc. on, until you learn how everything works, thats what I did anyways.
When you actually start a game up though, make sure to get yourself "Grants".
Grants are basically just Quests that give you the money you need, and set a basis for what you should have in your prison. Most of your income will come from it at first.
Also I recommend not using the default prisoner income, I do about 6. Also make sure you have proper security if your taking on max security prisoners, some could have the "extreemly volitial" triat, and will regularly kill people, attack people, destroy things, etc.
The game is a lot of fun, if you like tycoons and managing stuff, this is a must have.

One of the best built open world games I've had the pleasure of exploring. You wouldn't expect the desert to be so varied, fascinating, beautiful, glorious and colorful. From sand dunes to rock canyons to wide plains of dirt, to ruined cities and highways, to trash mountains and more. And the navigation is very engaging, the vehicles are beasts, very varied and powerful, even from the start of the game. Hand to hand combat borrowed from Assassin's Creed and Arkham series, but implemented very uniquely and satisfying. You're Mad Max, the legend, the boogie-man of the Australian wastes. So glad to play a game outside of U.S.A. that isn't as drab as the Metro or Stalker series, or as satirical as the Just Cause games. The soul of this game is in the relics. Max's comments on found relics break your heart sometimes. Max's story has always been a story about loss and revenge and I think this game captured both very well. I've tried to make the experience last as long as possible. I believe it still has a lot of gas left in the tank. Please announce a goddang sequel already!

I loved Absolution. This plays a lot like Absolution BUT is a little harder. It is still very playable but you really must do your homework before just blasting people in the face. That said...
It was WAY too short. It took me 2 hours (a good player would have it done in 1 hour) to complete the training mission and the ONE mission you get for $14.99. Luckily my friend got it for me on sale (ty) but even still.
I can not see buying the rest until maybe the entire package is around $30. I had fun I really did. This was not even close to enough content to justify the cost.
If this is what I have to go on, expecting maybe 1-3 hours of gameplay per mission, then for a total of $60 you might get 15-20 of game time if you are just playing the missions, which is all I primarily do. I try to aim for a avg of $ 2-3/ hr on a game. Some shoot for $5/hr. Your milage may vary.
The only way this is even worth the cost is for those die hard completionists that will play the mission 17 times to unlock the challenges.
I do NOT recommend buying this solely on the basis that there does not appear to be enough content for the asking price.
Graphics- 4/5 - running my 980 with a 4.4 ghz OC 8320, I ran into some bottleneck somewhere. Probably CPU. I was able to get 60fps in 1080p MOST of the time. It looks pretty good and runs well but it is very taxing and hard to maintain 60 when things pop off or a lot is happening. I had to turn a lot of the settings down below high to avg 55 in game. The cutscenes were massively improved in quality from Absolution. The lighting effects were not to my liking and some of the textures just seemed very dull. The character models were very good.
Sound- 4/5 - Not much to say here. Nothing special. Nothing wrong with it. Dialog sounded good, sound effects were good. A slight improvement in some areas from the last game.
Gameplay- 3/5 I started using mouse and keyboard but found xbox 360 controller to be much easier. There was a few issues with sticking to cover at random and some general jankiness that was uncomfortable at times. I could control my walk speed and direction much easier on the controller than the m/kb. Otherwise, it takes what I liked about Absolution and added some new challenges. Patience is certainly required. I gave it a 3 because it was not as smooth overall as the last game and felt rushed in some aspects. For the price, I would have expected a lot more to be polished. A lot could be worked out such as janky controls and some of the AI is less than stellar. It is very playable. It took a few steps forward and a few steps back IMO in quality of gameplay.
Overall - 3/5 I am factoring in price, time spent, and quality of product. Think of this as the Madden of stealth games. Its a "new roster", some "new grass" and a "new gameplay mechanic" but that is about it. Also they want more money for less content. I really don't think its worth what they want even if it is AAA.
tl;dr
AAA status should not automatically get you a $60 price tag. You have to deliver something worth that much money, and I just don't believe this is worth it.

Slick and responsive twin-stick shooter with a bright, colorful, and psychedelic visual style and a very intuitive and addictive dashing mechanic. Each dash ends with a powerful burst obliterating any nearby baddies with an extremely satisfying explosion, and is crucial in the most chaotic of moments.
The sound design kept my ears perked at all times just as any authentic arcade experience should, with distinct bleeps of power ups being collected and the tinkling of small crystalline enemies spawning from their red-glowing silhouette. Trigonarium is a twin-stick that just bleeds with awesome and nostalgic atmosphere.
The gameplay starts off slowly in usual twin-stick fashion with smaller enemies casually lurching around you from each corner, but as time goes on and score conditions are met the frequency and intensity of waves increases into a seriously chaotic cluster♥♥♥♥ of colorfully calculated craziness. Things get tense to the point where you're counting down every second until your next Dash move is charged to plow your way forcefully to that crucial power-up that just spawned across the map.
Trigonarium is an incredibly charming and inventive, extremely fun to play twin-stick and is criminally underpriced given the amount of fun I've squeezed out of it.

Campaign mode is *big*, with varied bosses separated by plenty of waves of enemies. The enemies in these waves and their spawn locations are vastly different and much more intense in the harder game mode, it's not just "the same again but your gun is 50% weaker."
It's all topped off with fair but difficult achievements, and plenty of replayability for quick-fix or endurance sessions.
Grab it, I'd recommend it without hesitation.

A short, personal story.
One of the worst things about sexual harassment and assault (other than, y'know... their existence) is their banality. They aren’t something that happens only in places and times of great remoteness and high drama, beyond the walls of everyday experience… they are (at present, though hopefully not forever) a part of the landscape. And it’s a part of the landscape that many of us never experience and get to look past if we choose.
Freeman has a solid history of using interactive media to capture and communicate true-ringing life experiences: youth and innocent curiosity in 'how do you Do It?,' illness, body image, and anxiety in 'Mangia,' romance in cyber- & meat-space in 'Cibele.' I think my first interaction with her work was ‘Space Dad’ from Space Cowboy Jam 2014, which uses a simple game structure to tell a framed story of a young girl imagining what her often on the road trucker father’s life is like. Deceptively simple, but clearly heartfelt. That is, I think, how I would boil down all of Freeman’s work that I’ve played so far:

If you see people saying Origins is horribad, rest assured, they're wrong.
First thing first, Origins is almost copy paste of Arkham City, the 2nd installment of Arkham series. It definitely brings many good things Arkham City (and Asylum) had. Similar gadgets, similar combat styles, familiar characters (well, of course, it's Batman after all), and it's always nice to know Batman before he became established super hero. If you've played the previous two, you wouldn't feel any awkwardness playing the game.
Navigating in an open city couldn't be easier. Batman can jump from building to building, grapple with ease - much ease than on AC from my fingers' memory - and now can use 'teleport' aka fast travel with Batwing to reach other corners faster. ...well uh, after completing Tower missions against Enigma, of course.
There are also many other hidden objects and sidequests you can do like in Arkham City. Enigma Datapack, destroying poison barrels etc. The template pretty much the same like previous installment
Personal preference: I've played all three Batman installments on Steam, and I feel the smoothest combat is from this Origins.
Performance wise, so far I am having zero problem with Batman Origins set up on all low settings. On Batman Arkham City, though, I've had considerable slowdown, not because of my weak graphic card, but because it was bugged game engine - thanks to PhysX.
For the contents on Steam aka DLC, there's zero reason to get multiplayer DLCs. This game's intended to be played as SINGLE player. Why on earth would they be pushing MP contents into Batman I don't know. Just buy the SP DLCs and you're good to go, or wait until GOTY pops up. By that time, then, I think Arkham Knight will have been in existence. Game's on sale for 75% off quite often, so I would recommend to pick it up at that price.
And don't forget, this game's best played with controller. I have no issue with both Dinput (using x360ce) and Xinput gamepads.
So yeah, Arkham Origins is the game you either hate or love. It's a copy paste from previous game, and adds almost nothing except better combat and or navigation in city, perhaps. Well what can I say, don't fix what ain't broken? Isn't that the golden rule?
At any rate, this game is a must have if you're Batman fans.

Spec Ops: The Line is a solid modern military cover third person shooter set in Dubai.  The game is on the somewhat shorter side, taking about a dozen hours at higher difficulties to finish.  For the most satisfying experience do not try to blitz through it at difficulties below Suicide Mission.  Playing on FUBAR difficulty is something else altogether.  It will be frustrating, and you will play some parts of the game maybe a dozen times in a row before you finally manage to stay alive through it, but the frustration only adds to the experience.  This is not your cookie cutter shooter about a western soldier putting evil eastern villains to the gun in heroic fashion. It's a game about a soldier having to kill fellow soldiers and worse.  It's about getting frustrated with having to kill until you literally have no choice but stop giving a ♥♥♥♥ altogether.  The storytelling is nothing short of genius and by the time it all comes together it will leave you with a twisted satisfaction and a feeling that you've experienced a new narrative standard in video games.  This is the best game I played in half a decade, maybe even longer.  Buy it, play it and keep asking yourself if you feel like a hero yet.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding lemon bars recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1) 2 cups Flour
2) 1/2 cup Sugar
3) 1/4 teaspoon Salt
4) 2 sticks (1 Cup) Salted Butter, Cut Into Small Cubes
5) Filling
6) 1-1/2 cup Sugar
7) 1/4 cup Flour
8) 4 whole Large Eggs
9) Zest And Juice Of 4 Medium-sized Lemons
10) Powdered Sugar, For Sifting
Directions:
1. For the crust: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Grease a 9-by-13-inch pan with butter.
2. Stir together the flour, sugar, and salt. Add the butter to the bowl and use a pastry cutter to cut it all together until the mixture resembles fine crumbs. Press into the prepared pan and bake until golden around the edges, about 20 minutes.
3. For the filling: Stir together the sugar and flour. Crack in the eggs and whisk to combine. Add the lemon zest and juice and mix until combined. Pour over the crust and bake about 20 minutes.
4. Allow to cool in the fridge for a minimum of 2 hours, then sift powdered sugar over the top before cutting into squares.
(Use an 8 x 10 pan if you'd like the layers to be a little thicker.)

Hi there ! You've probably never even heard of Kung Fu Strike. So... welcome, join the club ! If you want a cool, cel shaded sort of beat 'em up, this might just be the thing for you. It surprised me, in a positive way. Having never heard of the game it's usually difficult to judge if a certain game might be in your alley. Kung Fu Strike could be.
KFS manages to give us smooth controls (very important for a beat 'em up), sharp visuals, ok sounds (nothing extraordinary) and solid gameplay.
The story isn't all that great, but the battles are. Most of the times. Each level consists of 4 smaller levels with the fourth one having a boss battle. These boss battles can be pretty hard if you just mash the buttons so in order to win you'll have to create combos, deflect attacks and use chi energy, in a tactical way. Trust me, it's not as easy as it sounds. But hey, I like a challenge so I'll just keep trying I guess.
Anyway, you might actually want to put this little game on your radar people.

This game pretty much describes my times in Middle School and High School. Almost everyday I played this game in Middle School, but the hours have mellowed in High School after my interests in traditional art and my expansion to newer interests. Originally got it on my first laptop from my old account (that I forgot the password to). I remember the update was 1.0.5, (wasn’t it the rocket boots update?) and my PC pretty much crapped out on me after a few weeks when I bought the game. Around 2012-2013, the game came out for Xbox 360, my lil mind just nutted 50 times. This was the beginning of the addiction on overdrive.
I bought the game on the Xbox 360, everyday after school, I would play Terraria 12 hours a day during summer. I would invite my friend over to eventually conquer hardmode (pre-Plantera update). During the Summer between 8th-9th grade, I got myself a new Laptop. And then I forgot my old account, so I created a new Steam Account, mostly because it was on my Dad’s email. I bought Terraria again, but didn’t play it on the PC until 1.2. I’d play bits of it on the PC, but I was so used to the Xbox controls, I decided to stick with the Xbox 360.
Eventually that PC craps out, and then I waited a whole year until I finally get a new PC. 1.2 just came out a week ago and I was borrowing mom’s PC. I got Steam, downloaded Terraria, a few weeks later mom starts arguing with me that Steam is a virus. I use her Norton Antivirus and MacAfee to scan the PC, no virus was unveiled, but Norton says MacAfee and BigFishGames maybe a threat. I kinda just ignored those messages, not wanting to mess with her stuff. Next year, she passed the PC down to me, I don’t play games as much anymore due to my new found for art.
I factory reset the junky PC, redownloaded Steam, and play Terraria for mostly nostalgic reasons. I could review it by update, but I was gone for most of the 1.2 updates. This game has changed a lot in art style and design, but the gameplay has always stayed true to its original idea. Explore, Loot, Dig. The main three components of the game.
Exploring is probably the most important part of Terraria in my opinion, I simple can’t start a game with a character prepackaged with the essentials. I want to go out and have the troubles of the beginning, scraping for the best of items early on. I always rush to the Dungeon after I get a full set of iron armor for the chance of a water bolt. I check every detail in the earth now to locate the enchanted sword shrines. I’ve played the game enough to know what to do and what to get.
Looting has always been a treat, makes me feel awarded whenever I open hold chest. Sadly that joy fades away very quickly right when you enter hardmode. Chests are relatively useless in hardmode (unless you count the biome chests). But enemy loot is almost always useful, even if you’re in the deepest ends of hardmode. I understand why there are no hardmode chests in the underground, but a chest feels more magical than a loot drop, yet a loot drop feels more rewarding.
Digging, you’ll be doing that a lot in this game, get used to it. (Unless you get lucky).
Is this game good? Heck yeah! If you’re looking for a goodtime with friends or just by yourself, I’d recommend this game. I’d give this game a 8.7/10, real good!

People call it a minecraft rip-off but it has WAY more stuff to do than minecraft. I perticularly love fighting all the diferent bosses, but the rest of the game is still really good! (e.g. building a better house, exploring the your world, etc) overall I would defiitely recommend.

Need to update this with more info, so ill give a brief summary of what I said before.
I love hitman, always have. Its a game that was born after a night of drinking between max payne and a 007 spy movie and has spent most of its childhood trying to decide what parent it wanted to be more like.
Now we have this one, with alot of my favorite features removed but plenty added in too. Dual weilding, carrying in a sawed off shotgun, the gun filled hideout you can steal weapons off to, gone. In is an easy to use system to pursue paths to kill targets replacing the tumble around in the dark trying not to die system from the last games. In are ugly guns with ugly violet coloring and ugly skins you dont want to unlock because the guns are ugly and you cant conceal them in a suitcase.
Now that sounds negative, but lets be clear. this game is all the good absolution had to offer and all the bad gone and forgotten. Back to reality, 47. Back to assassinating and missions and different approaches and all the stuff you loved about the early games. Hopefully the coming seasons will add more stuff from the old games that we missed (gimme back my bloody sawn-off, will ya?) Long story short, we can pretend that absolution was a tech demo and this was the game meant to follow up on blood money.
My review was formerly negative, mostly because im incapable of being pleased. But now, IO is on its own, an independant company with no big backer. Thats a nasty move by their overlords, leaving them like that just as they got back to making good games, but IO didnt sell out or ditch the rights to hitman, they held onto it, and now, they dont have the safety cushion of a big company backing them. That means in plain speak that HITMAN season 2 and forward will be their sweat and tears for their livelihood. I do believe we should support them and in return we should expect better content than ever before. This is a company we grew up with, Ive owned more hitman games than any other franchise, I know which game companies I want to keep alive and that have earned a right to my loyalty.
So yes, review is positive now, and I will be getting the second season the moment I can should they manage to get it out. Good luck IO, your fans love you.

This game has very few rules.
1.  Hold prisoners for thier allotted time.
2. Try not to get too many killed in any one day.
3.  Profit.
This is a management sim/sandbox. Primarily, you will be building and designing rooms, managing your employees, and running an intelegence network.  How your prisoners are treated is really up to you; you can be the reformer or the punisher.
Gameplay itself can be changed when you first create a new prison.  You can choose your warden, prisoner genders, gang presence, weather effect, and random events.
Even though Prisoner Achitect is out of early access, the developers still add content every now and then.  Be sure to check the community page when you see an update and check out their announcement and demonstration video.
Edit:  Since I posted this review, the developers issued thier final update (giving dev shortcuts).  The game has taken on a different dynamic for me.   While it was in early access, I would essentially be playing a new prison with a new challenge level every month as it was updated.   I think that was the most fun for me.  I still love the game, but expect this to be the finished article.  It's wonderful and challenging, but not as dynamic as an experience as it was in early access.

Ori and the Blind Forest is a platfomer, with Metroid-like backtracking and upgrades. In many respects, it's like Axiom Verge or more closely, Strider from a few years ago. If you've played either of those games, you know what to expect here.
If not, basically there is a skill tree with 3 branches; certain doors and areas are locked until you reach a certain point in the story or you acquire the requisite skill; and there plenty of collectibles and secrets hidden behind false walls that you need to collect to achieve 100% completion.
Ori differentiates itself by being very aesthetically pleasing-- the game looks very striking, almost like an animated painting. It is an ideal game for taking screenshots or recording videos.
The gameplay is the other main draw for me (and most people); thanks to highly responsive controls and a varied (but always useful) moveset that evolves as you progress through the game, Ori is always a good challenge and lots of fun. I personally set it on Hard because I wanted an even greater challenge. If your truly a masochist, the game offers a One Life mode, where as the title implies, you can only die once.
The story is nice and charming but its really just a framework for the gameplay. It is just your basic good vs evil premise. The main protagonist is separated from the heart of the forest and must find its way back and restore order.
Overall, if you enjoy good platforming games and can enjoy a Disney-esqe story, I would wholeheartedly recommend this game.

The Definitive Edition added the chapter of Naru, and two extra skills for Ori. The issue of map sealed have been improved in this version, players are allowed to continue the game after finishing the whole story. Beautiful and excellent, my favorite 2D game this year.

Overall - Complicated Review here
Score: 7/10
Game will challenge your thinking about the FPS genre a bit and force you to make decisions that may come during realistic situations as perhaps depicted in the game. The voice acting, sound, etc, is pretty good. The game is immersive. Sometimes you fight the controls. The story will keep you going even if the game play starts to peter out. Game has won awards... All that being said, I wouldn't recommend it. Normally I recommend everything over a score of 5. I did not like the game. Below if you want reasons. Game has been bundled, I would never pay full price.
Story: The story is interesting and unique and pits the player in an interesting situation where they are under the assumption that they will be helping in a crisis area. Characters are believable and you can relate to them. However, I didn't actually enjoy the story.
Gameplay: Realistic type FPS. Personally that's a no go for me typically. If you like that type of FPS, then this game is probably a bit more for you, however the controls will still leave you wanting. Harder difficulties may end up with enemies being bullet sponges. Cause that's fun.
Audio: Overall, this was definitely my favorite part. I enjoyed the voice acting and the music. It was always appropriate to what the developers were trying to convey during the story.
Graphics: Game is a bit dated, but still the graphics were good for this style of game. They'd probably be a bit better if I had a better card, but with what I had, I was content.
Final Notes: While the game was innovative and definitely an experience, I didn't really enjoy it and therefore wouldn't recommend it even though technically it hits all the marks to be recommended. I went into it not knowing anything about the game, and came out understanding why it was a commercial failure but still received(was nominated for?) awards.
If you're looking for something different, and don't have my issues as listed above, then get the game and give it a go, but if you are looking for a good time, and to enjoy a story and not deal with cognitive dissonance, take a pass.

I played this game to the maximum possible completion and I got to say, where was the effort? On the surface there is nothing wrong with the game, aside from rare but annoying 'getting-stuck-on-nothing' glitches. The problem is that there was a little bit more they could have done. For example, motorbikes! In every mad max movie ever there have always been motorbikes, and big rigs and my personal favorite, light aircraft. With only the slightest bit more effort there could have been so much more to this game that would have made it great, rather than meh. The leveling system was not balanced (I maxed out all the griffa things after my second zone) and tying vehicle upgrades with plot events make some of them useless before you even get them. The scrap currency was too plentiful and [Spoiler Alert!] I feel there was a lack of enthusiasm when it came to the ending, hell the main plot itself seemed way too short and somewhat rushed. As for things to do, I ran out at like 60 hours. I would like to see this game get an update one day that addresses these shortfalls but I fear not. Like so many others it became a half a*sed movie based game that (like so many others) failed to deliver. In my opinion only just though, there was a lot of research done and the whole collecting things made the world a tiny bit more immersive. Oh and one last thought, the driving control scheme sucks balls. I give it a 4/10 it had potential but was just a cash grab after all

a surprisingly good game. all this time I thought it was a mediocre game (as with most Movie inspired/adaptation/tie-in games) so I never bothered to even check it out, I was wrong.
I added it to my growing list of backlogs after a quick look on it during a sale and reading the 90% positive reviews. When I finally got into playing it, I was surprised. It's a nice fresh take on the open world third person action adventure genre. The game combines many different and popular mechanics from other similar games together with their own original ones that resulted into a great game. You see some slight Batman Arkham fighting mechanics, some Assassins Creed exploration/mission styles, and it's got some Fallout/Metro 2033 vibes going on. in additional to the game's unique Vehicle combat and customization ~ There's ALOT of driving in this game. You own a car, the "magnum opus", it's your main car throughout the game, and you can upgrade it, customize it with defenses, weapons, and cosmetics, tune its performance, etc. getting better and better as you progress throughout missions. Tons of side-missions to complete aside from the main story line, so they really took their time in creating a full open world experience.
The map is big, kinda empty(the game is set in a desert wasteland after all), but still has enough content in between so you don't get bored while driving. the graphics are AMAZING, it still looks like it came today, and the game is well polished for a game based on a movie, not too mention it runs so well compared to other similar games. The story is decent, not too great but not bad either. It kinda compares to the story of Mad Max: Fury Road (the movie). by the way, it isn't related at all to the movie. It just shares the universe and the settings, but the story is fully stand-alone, hell, even Mad Max looks different here from the movies(Mel Gibson and Tom Hardy).
Again, The game has one of the most epic and awesome intro's I've ever seen. and the gameplay didn't disappoint either. My only issues in the game are the game checkpoints that's messed up, sometimes you die and you spawn way too far in the game both in the progression and in the world map, also and that cutscenes, (e.g. when dying in a boss fight so the game loads that part again) cannot be skipped. Lastly the controls are kinda weird, it's very different from your typical third person controls, took me some time to get used to.

Where can I begin when describing this masterpiece?  From the moment you are transplanted into the cab of a powerful European Truck (not to be confused with those wussy American trucks) you will be hooked!  Speaking of hooking, trailer hitching is so realistic!  I had to wipe the beads of sweat off my brow after the furious 10 second leadup to pressing T to connect the trailer.  It was VERY INTENSE.

I still hit the car, resulting in a small fine and no visible damage to my truck, which is again the utmost in realistic simulation action.
Europe is painstakingly mapped, featuring realistic rocks and trees and two or more roads per country that connect both of the major cities.  And you have the choice of delivering meat, cheese, milk, and other important European commodities.  Such diversity of experience.  It is an endless source of wonderment that represents the pinnacle of modern video gaming.

This game has very few rules.
1.  Hold prisoners for thier allotted time.
2. Try not to get too many killed in any one day.
3.  Profit.
This is a management sim/sandbox. Primarily, you will be building and designing rooms, managing your employees, and running an intelegence network.  How your prisoners are treated is really up to you; you can be the reformer or the punisher.
Gameplay itself can be changed when you first create a new prison.  You can choose your warden, prisoner genders, gang presence, weather effect, and random events.
Even though Prisoner Achitect is out of early access, the developers still add content every now and then.  Be sure to check the community page when you see an update and check out their announcement and demonstration video.
Edit:  Since I posted this review, the developers issued thier final update (giving dev shortcuts).  The game has taken on a different dynamic for me.   While it was in early access, I would essentially be playing a new prison with a new challenge level every month as it was updated.   I think that was the most fun for me.  I still love the game, but expect this to be the finished article.  It's wonderful and challenging, but not as dynamic as an experience as it was in early access.

This game is highly recommended from me.
I would describe this game as a throughly enjoyable drive across Europe if you're into driving simulators like this one. You get opportunities to create & own your own trucking company by having your own garage or by owning multiple garages if you're seriously that ambitious business wise, buying a large fleet of trucks, hiring your own drivers as employees & by getting paid an evergrowing serious amount of money (not real of course) from other contracting companies by completing deliveries on time to various delivery spots around Europe.
You're given a chance to do this by taking out a bank loan, which is optional by the way, which is dependable on the amount  of money in your bank balance from your completed deliveries from A to B. Or you can save up your own money to buy stuff for your business instead but that is if you want decision yourself. You can base your company garage from one of a multitude of countries around Europe that are available in the game from the beginning. You can add DLCs to the game to add more countries in it if you wish.
Once you carry out deliveries; you start off doing small contract work to give a stepping stone in building up your reputation as a law-abiding & compentent truck driver. You do have to obey road traffic laws & speed limits in roads of each country you visit in the game otherwise you will be subject to speeding fines & fines for being involved in road accidents along your journey.
While you're driving your truck; you can do things like adjust seats, mirrors, lighting on the outside of the truck. You can also listen to music from your mp3s stored on your computer or by listening to live streamed internet radio stations just by pressing R on your computer keyboard.
The other good thing about this game is that keeps itself contantly updated all the time every time you play it on Steam. You can also add updates from the games official website to update to the latest version but that is entirely up to yourself.
Once you set up your company; make sure you set up an online World of Trucks account for yourself to help gain achievements in that account. You can link both ETS2 & American Truck Simulator in the same account.
I will also say that sadly the game is not saved on the steam cloud. You would have to back up your files on another external cloud service or from an external hard drive or solid state drive to save your progress.
If you're into trucks & into driving games; have a go at this game if you feel you can be successful at it. Happy trucking.

Really, this game has something for everyone. Dedicated builders will have a field day with the advanced wiring system and huge customizability. People looking for a adventure game will be the most pleased; in my opinion: That's really the core of Terraria and what makes it so goddamn enjoyable. It seems like a Minecraft ripoff when you first start it: Cutting trees to get wood to make a house to survive to the next day.
But that all changes the moment you begin to descend. At first there are slimes that give you gel to get torches. You go "Meh, seems okay so far..." But the game really begins to shine when you find a rare enemy or get lucky from a rare drop or loot some chests.
And now the game picks up momentum and never stops. You rampage through the enemies who have no chance against your rare weapon. Then you realise that you are a glass cannon, doing great damage but have no defense at all.
Cue Crystal Heart finding, Armor crafting and dangerous quests for ore. Cue intense bossfights, item hunting, mobility upgrading, and hardmode... Cue hours and hours of enjoyment!

PURE. UNADULTERATED. PLATFORM BLISS.
Super Meat Boy is one hell of an adrenaline rush and by calling it that is an understatement!  You follow your tale throughout Team Meat's adventure as Meat Boy which is basically a cube of meat...that's not surprisingly a boy. His quest to take back his dearly beloved lady, Bandage Girl, from the evil cluthes of Dr. Fetus is an exciting tale of anguish, but determination. As Meat Boy trudges through the 300+ innovative and unrelenting stages based on the retro platformers of yesteryear, he meets some fellow characters from other popular Flash Games such as Commander Video (Bit Trip Runner) and The Kid (I Want To Be The Guy) that can be used with their special abilities to better or even undermine you in levels.
Be forwarned: THIS GAME IS HARD AS BALLS. You'll die, and die, and die, and probably even throw your pc out the window into the nearest freaking land heep of other computers that have been throwed out due to this game, but don't let this heed stop you from experiencing this. One thing to surely take from this game is how fair this aneurysm enducing experience is. The controls are precisely fined tuned and butter smooth which is heavily important in a twitch platforming game such as this. Even though this game boils down to being as hard as nails (especially apparent in later levels), each death is fair and most of the time caused by the player, him/herself, but with each and every nerve indusing calamity, it'll help you get a better grip and understanding of how to succeed in further attemps and better you in the future. For whenever you do conquer that one obstacle that's been blocking your way to success, the sense of accomplishment is unparalled and unrivaled. And before long, you'll be flying through with ease and flair like it's second nature!
Graphics are nailed right down to the very center. Nostalgia is definitely an apparent factors as the art style is showcased in gnarly 16 bit fashion. This is carried even further as the bonus secret warp zone stages are brought forth in pure 8 bit style. Worth mentioning are the multiple worlds that you progress though and the levels that follow. Each world has a specific theme that let's the player know where your hero is venturing off into. Each and every level follows through to that suit of representation which really makes you relate to Meat Boy for each and every scenario he ends up getting in.
I can't recommend this game enough! Video game references abound along with a plethora of snazzy, platforming stages to occupy one for days. This is the game that you should be letting your newborn play after he exits the womb. Or even after you Ram Jam your significant other, this is defintely the sweet spot of entertainment. So go out there bucko! No matter who you are, you'll definitely find something charming enough to warrant a purchase of Super Meat Boy.

I'm really not sure how this got to be popular. The driving feels far too heavy to be enjoyable, even for a simulator, and there are so, so many bugs in the physics engine and the AI's control of their vehicles for me to avoid running out of money while transporting goods.
The AI change lanes as fast as the cars on the freeways in GTA: San Andreas did - i.e. faster than your lumbering starter truck could ever hope to. They do so even when you are in the lane, which forces you to slam on the brakes lest you rear end them, leaving their car totally uninjured (i mean, really? we had destructable car models years and years ago) and immobile in the middle of the freeway. This often causes pileups as although your brakes are terrible, the AI's brakes are worse.
The character model is horribly dated, even for 2008 - while your truck is quite a pretty piece of graphics, the character driving it has a grand total of three different animations - "turn left, turn right, not turning", and they jar horribly if you're viewing the vehicle from the front.
It appears to be very, very quickly churned out by a junior company for a driving school, not a full fledged trucking game which I hoped.

a surprisingly good game. all this time I thought it was a mediocre game (as with most Movie inspired/adaptation/tie-in games) so I never bothered to even check it out, I was wrong.
I added it to my growing list of backlogs after a quick look on it during a sale and reading the 90% positive reviews. When I finally got into playing it, I was surprised. It's a nice fresh take on the open world third person action adventure genre. The game combines many different and popular mechanics from other similar games together with their own original ones that resulted into a great game. You see some slight Batman Arkham fighting mechanics, some Assassins Creed exploration/mission styles, and it's got some Fallout/Metro 2033 vibes going on. in additional to the game's unique Vehicle combat and customization ~ There's ALOT of driving in this game. You own a car, the "magnum opus", it's your main car throughout the game, and you can upgrade it, customize it with defenses, weapons, and cosmetics, tune its performance, etc. getting better and better as you progress throughout missions. Tons of side-missions to complete aside from the main story line, so they really took their time in creating a full open world experience.
The map is big, kinda empty(the game is set in a desert wasteland after all), but still has enough content in between so you don't get bored while driving. the graphics are AMAZING, it still looks like it came today, and the game is well polished for a game based on a movie, not too mention it runs so well compared to other similar games. The story is decent, not too great but not bad either. It kinda compares to the story of Mad Max: Fury Road (the movie). by the way, it isn't related at all to the movie. It just shares the universe and the settings, but the story is fully stand-alone, hell, even Mad Max looks different here from the movies(Mel Gibson and Tom Hardy).
Again, The game has one of the most epic and awesome intro's I've ever seen. and the gameplay didn't disappoint either. My only issues in the game are the game checkpoints that's messed up, sometimes you die and you spawn way too far in the game both in the progression and in the world map, also and that cutscenes, (e.g. when dying in a boss fight so the game loads that part again) cannot be skipped. Lastly the controls are kinda weird, it's very different from your typical third person controls, took me some time to get used to.

If you're looking for a game, you should probably turn around now. This point and click story has only one good thing: Pretty art. You are pesented with a false sense of choice with typically two options in different screens. One is more of introvert, the other an extrovert. You essentially decide whether or not you are going to wear make-up, and then if you should wait for your buddy Jenna. Inevitably, the bouncer assaults you, which is about the only confronting part of this project. After that, you're traumatised. The end.
Now, it's not that the we should invalidate the story. This is based off actual events. Horrible things happened to the developer. That being said, it's a sort of story that works better as an animation rather than a series of circumstantial multiple choice questions. The person 'playing' ultimately does not 'win' regardless of which path is taken. There is no actual point to offering more than one answer, because the conclusion and the story format is always the same. It also seems a little confusing to offer more than one answer when this idea is autobiographical. If we are invited into her story, it seems it would make more sense to keep this to a single, straight line for the events unfolding. If the idea is that no matter what happens, the character is not prepared for the assault from the bouncer, then perhaps instead of two questions resulting in the same thing, multiple options should have been made available. What if we waited for Jenna to return? What if we got the option to not drink? Of course, that would be breaking from the autobiography of this tale.
My final issue with this is who is the intended audience? I assume it's for everyone. Are we looking to learn the devestation of sexual assault, or are we just meant to sympathise and relate to Nina? I would advise people who are genuinely triggered by these themes to not 'play' this. There's nothing here for someone looking to deal with it to gain any sense of empathy, it's just the telling of a story. With that being said, I have been put into situations where this sort of thing has nearly happened, and this thing left a sour taste in my mouth. If you want to call it art, that's your perogative, but that doesn't really excuse how disappointing this thing was. I like to think Nina is doing better now, but I'm sorry, this just bothered me.

That said, it’s easy to tell who's hacking and who the actual good players are and there are lots btw.  The game does get repetitve after a while, I find its best in few hour sessions when I don't feel like playing my main game.
Money is reasonably easy come by, you can ram-raid shops as a crim or just do the pvp missioning system which forms the core gameplay. If you get bored of that you can always grab a dump truck and go have fun grefing up people’s missions, although that sounds bad there are very strict mechanics in play that prevent constant greifing most of the time.
APB is a lot of fun if you are prepared to spend a few dollars for a couple of guns (the NTEC scoped is my fav) and has given me and my friends many hours of entertainment compared to the cost. Try it out, hang in there longer then the first 15 minutes or so and let it sink in and you will be rewarded with a fun casual game in your library.

Ah DmC DmC DmC... where to begin with you, my lovely reboot. Whilst the entire fanbase and the general public foam at the mouth at the thought of Dante being an eccentric, over the top tough guy with a superiority complex and a disregard for authority... sorry, that's an explanation of Dante. What I mean to say is that they foam at the mouth because he doesn't look like a pretty boy Japanese Anime Character and white hair.
Complaints flood the internet about the storyline of DmC and how it is "stupid" or "nonsensical". I wholeheartedly agree, it's a ridiculous storyline but since when was DMC revered for its storyline? From all the DMC titles I've played, there never has been a great storyline. It's the combat, action and visuals that people want, and DmC delivers with a SSSensational result.
Combat is the best. There. I said it. No other DMC title has combat that flows so well together. The visuals and art style are brilliant, with the demonic affected 'Limbo' worlds tearing apart as reality collapses around you. Enemies are fast and deadly and whilst it may seem easy to tear up the goons and hit a solid SS rank, the higher the difficulty then the harder it is to maintain those top ranks.
Music also kicks in. DMC4 had one basic tune for the majority of the battle fights whereas DmC constantly kicks you in the nuts with Combichrist & Noisia tracks that really do suit the absurdity of the situation Dante is in. Yes. I'm gushing over this game. I used to really rip into this title with D0nT3 & his bro VIRG1n but I can't help but smile and realise that buying this game was money well spent. I haven't had such a good time on a DMC title before, heck I enjoy this more than I did with DMC3.
If you want a true opinion then don't search for it online. Take it from me, the game is brilliant and the replayability is geared at 500%, you'll find yourself coming back for more and more and more. I know I will. This is definately a worthwhile purchase. Don't buy Dead Space 3. Buy DmC instead. 8/10!

a surprisingly good game. all this time I thought it was a mediocre game (as with most Movie inspired/adaptation/tie-in games) so I never bothered to even check it out, I was wrong.
I added it to my growing list of backlogs after a quick look on it during a sale and reading the 90% positive reviews. When I finally got into playing it, I was surprised. It's a nice fresh take on the open world third person action adventure genre. The game combines many different and popular mechanics from other similar games together with their own original ones that resulted into a great game. You see some slight Batman Arkham fighting mechanics, some Assassins Creed exploration/mission styles, and it's got some Fallout/Metro 2033 vibes going on. in additional to the game's unique Vehicle combat and customization ~ There's ALOT of driving in this game. You own a car, the "magnum opus", it's your main car throughout the game, and you can upgrade it, customize it with defenses, weapons, and cosmetics, tune its performance, etc. getting better and better as you progress throughout missions. Tons of side-missions to complete aside from the main story line, so they really took their time in creating a full open world experience.
The map is big, kinda empty(the game is set in a desert wasteland after all), but still has enough content in between so you don't get bored while driving. the graphics are AMAZING, it still looks like it came today, and the game is well polished for a game based on a movie, not too mention it runs so well compared to other similar games. The story is decent, not too great but not bad either. It kinda compares to the story of Mad Max: Fury Road (the movie). by the way, it isn't related at all to the movie. It just shares the universe and the settings, but the story is fully stand-alone, hell, even Mad Max looks different here from the movies(Mel Gibson and Tom Hardy).
Again, The game has one of the most epic and awesome intro's I've ever seen. and the gameplay didn't disappoint either. My only issues in the game are the game checkpoints that's messed up, sometimes you die and you spawn way too far in the game both in the progression and in the world map, also and that cutscenes, (e.g. when dying in a boss fight so the game loads that part again) cannot be skipped. Lastly the controls are kinda weird, it's very different from your typical third person controls, took me some time to get used to.

Review related to the October 2017 update (blueprints 3.0). Current date : October 12th 2017.
Been playing the game on and off since Legacy.
Most of the negative reviews you see that focus on this update don't do the game justice. Earlier updates progressively turned the game into a 24-hour PUBG-like, focused heavily on PvP with advanced weaponry available immediately after a server wipe.
The latest update reintroduced something that had been previously removed from the game : progression. A much requested and needed part of the game which is, as too many people forgot or didn't know, a Survival game, and not a Battle Royale.
The so-called "grind" really only is progression. The grind isn't any more intensive than it was before. It just means that you have to actually use the lower-tier gear while you progress through the game before you can actually access rocket launchers and stuff (although this isn't all exactly true for big clans who aren't that much affected by the update, but that's another topic).
To be perfectly honest, Rust is in a much better stay than it was the past months. It's not perfect (it never was, probably won't ever be), what it needs right now is mainly number tweaking (costs for researching blueprints, craft, etc.).
tl;dr : Rust is slowly going back to what it originally was. Lots of recent players are showing discontent because they discovered Rust in a different state, and they liked it better that way.

I'm afraid my overall experience with the game has been far too negative to warrant a positive review.
First off: the good.
- Graphic: The game is visually stunning, smooth and very pleasant to look at.
- Sound: The soundtrack is spot on and all audio effects are great.
The bad.
- Story: For what i've played, the story of the game is ridiculously bland. [Minor Story Spoiler]
Now, in my eyes this is a very, very boring storyline that exists mainly to justify your adventures.
If you disagree, which is absolutely fine, try to tell any friend or person you know what the game's story is without having them laugh or be left extremely confused.
- Gameplay: Frustrating and tedious, put shortly.
The game feels like a mix of Super Meat Boy and Metroid, as in you roam around from point to point across multiple obstacles with a certain degree of difficulty involved, while you will eventually find statues that give you additional abilities and with a bunch of side pickups if you're interested to hunt for them.
Now, unlike SMB and metroid, Ori and the Blind Forest doesn't do a great job at telling you what or where are threats; this is caused by graphical clutter (as you may find enemies completely covered by the foreground) or by using different colors: initially purple means bad, which makes sense and helps recognize threats immediatly. Eventually you may find differently colored threats that are hard to recognize quickly (mostly due to the graphical clutter, again).
So you died...it will happen, especially as there are a few areas where the developers want you to die at least that one time, and you'll find yourself back to your save point.
Where is the save point? It's wherever you want! You're in charge of placing checkpoints!
While this seems like a great design choice at first, it turns out to be fairly tedious after a while mainly because you do not know what you will face next.
To create a checkpoint you'll need one unit of energy, which can be found in blue crystals scattered around the scenery, no energy = no checkpoint.
If you save sparingly enough, then you will always have a few units of energy to save pretty much anywhere, however the game does a very bad job at telling you when you should create a checkpoint.
Initially you'll find a crystal in locations where saving makes sense, which is how it should work, however after not much time you're left on your own in this regard, causing you to potentially save in terrible places or not save after you've been smashed by a falling rock, causing you to repeat a portion of the level.
Speaking of repetition, just like in metroid you'll notice there are a few areas you can't quite reach yet. Most of the times they aren't subtle at all and they serve as a reminder to come back once you unlock the ability required to reach it, which means you are bound to backtrack your steps.
Most times those areas are accessible after jumping past various obstacles, which is fine, however it may happen that you go through all obstacles just to discover you need an extra ability just to reach that sweet sweet power up, essentially removing the prize after beating the challenge.
Now, while roaming around and defeating enemies you will eventually be awarded an ability point, which can be used to improve your capabilities. In the definitive edition this system is a tad flawed: the 4th upgrade of the 3rd skill line (yes, the skill tree is made of three lines) is a bonus to an ability you unlock at the end of the game and you must get it in order to access other upgrades in that line, which is a TERRIBLE design choice (this isn't an issue in the normal version of the game). Of course there will be more upgrades for this new ability which will, obviously, be in between the ones you may want, instead of being at the end of the line. Because reasons!
You should buy this game if you don't mind frustrating games.
TLDR: a mix of super meat boy and metroid, visually stunning but frustrating gameplay and bland storyline.

I am probably never going to finish this game. If I were you, I would pay caution to the heavy amount of positive reviews for this game. I am going to get straight to the point: Mad Max is a digital embodiment of boredom.
The game does do several things right: It has great driving mechanics, the characters are interesting, the visuals and atmosphere are fantastic, and the game is extremely faithful to the Mad Max license.
However, the game is just so uninteresting. If you have played literally any open world game in the past 5 years, you have played this game already. It has all the typical sandbox nonsense: Liberating bases, gringing currency for upgrades, pointless decrease of enemy presence in increasingly arbitrary-feeling regions, and very little distinction between the countless cannon fodder you find.
The game also has sever pulsating problems: Stupid AI,♥♥♥♥♥♥easy combat which makes upgrades feel like they make no difference, a dull story, and one of the most dead-feeling open worlds I have ever seen.
The game just does nothing to distinguish itself from any other game of its genre. It does nothing special.
Final Rating:5/10
Verdict: Mad Max is a decent game with a solid foundation, but does nothing to build up the genre or hold interest with its bare-bones, painfully average gameplay.

At first glance, Spec Ops: The Line might seem to be another average shooter game, yet actually it is so much more than that. And despite the fact that I'm not really into military shooters, I enjoy playing this game. What can I say, an amazing story sets the pace with many unexpected twists and turns. This game shows perfectly all the brutality of war. The plot is constantly keeping you guessing and the ending is very mind blowing. Yes, some of it could be a little quirky, but it is still one of the best stories I've ever encountered. Also, the game has excellent character progression.
However, the 3rd-person shooter gameplay is pretty unimpressive: the cover system is temperamental, the aiming sucks, the weapons are boring, and stealth is rarely possible. It ends up being repetitive as do most cover-and-fire games. So, to be honest, the gameplay is nothing special and could be considered  quite bad, but I guess that is not what this game was made for.
The graphics are quite good, the soundtracks are also amazing and only bring more depth to the game. On top of that, the noise and effects are genuinely special, sounding real and effective. Furthermore, the voice acting is top-tier and sounds very real.
Overall, if you go into playing Spec Ops: The Line with the mindset that it is a run of the military shooter you will be disappointed, but if you play it looking for a game that's story is both gripping and thought provoking, try this out. Trust me, this shooter is an outstanding piece of art when it comes to terms of story and picture. Give this game a shot, it might change your perception of the whole genre more than its technically superior counterparts ever could.

In the first moments of Spec Ops: The Line nothing interesting happens: 3 idiots march into Dubai and kill some bad guys with rock music playing in the background. Soon Spec Ops breaks free from that and you start seeing the real horrors of Dubai, such as: slaughtered civilians and soldiers, massive graveyards and other horrific scenes. The main characters are Lugo, Adams and Cpt. Walker (you play as the Cpt.) all members of Delta Force, sent into Dubai to rescue civilians and a battalion, the Damned 33d and their leader, John Conrad. At first, the trio works together perfectly, but in the end, the guys are totally sick of each other, as everyone has a different opinion how things unfold for them and believe me, things do not unfold good. The narrative of this game is so ♥♥♥♥ing great that I can advise you only to buy it. It also features a MP mode but it's a cluster ♥♥♥♥.
Verdict: MP is a massive slaughterhouse and the gameplay is nothing special really, but what's really waiting for you in Dubai, is something you'll want to see for yourself. After playing through this game, you won't touch an army shooter for months. 9/10

I'm afraid my overall experience with the game has been far too negative to warrant a positive review.
First off: the good.
- Graphic: The game is visually stunning, smooth and very pleasant to look at.
- Sound: The soundtrack is spot on and all audio effects are great.
The bad.
- Story: For what i've played, the story of the game is ridiculously bland. [Minor Story Spoiler]
Now, in my eyes this is a very, very boring storyline that exists mainly to justify your adventures.
If you disagree, which is absolutely fine, try to tell any friend or person you know what the game's story is without having them laugh or be left extremely confused.
- Gameplay: Frustrating and tedious, put shortly.
The game feels like a mix of Super Meat Boy and Metroid, as in you roam around from point to point across multiple obstacles with a certain degree of difficulty involved, while you will eventually find statues that give you additional abilities and with a bunch of side pickups if you're interested to hunt for them.
Now, unlike SMB and metroid, Ori and the Blind Forest doesn't do a great job at telling you what or where are threats; this is caused by graphical clutter (as you may find enemies completely covered by the foreground) or by using different colors: initially purple means bad, which makes sense and helps recognize threats immediatly. Eventually you may find differently colored threats that are hard to recognize quickly (mostly due to the graphical clutter, again).
So you died...it will happen, especially as there are a few areas where the developers want you to die at least that one time, and you'll find yourself back to your save point.
Where is the save point? It's wherever you want! You're in charge of placing checkpoints!
While this seems like a great design choice at first, it turns out to be fairly tedious after a while mainly because you do not know what you will face next.
To create a checkpoint you'll need one unit of energy, which can be found in blue crystals scattered around the scenery, no energy = no checkpoint.
If you save sparingly enough, then you will always have a few units of energy to save pretty much anywhere, however the game does a very bad job at telling you when you should create a checkpoint.
Initially you'll find a crystal in locations where saving makes sense, which is how it should work, however after not much time you're left on your own in this regard, causing you to potentially save in terrible places or not save after you've been smashed by a falling rock, causing you to repeat a portion of the level.
Speaking of repetition, just like in metroid you'll notice there are a few areas you can't quite reach yet. Most of the times they aren't subtle at all and they serve as a reminder to come back once you unlock the ability required to reach it, which means you are bound to backtrack your steps.
Most times those areas are accessible after jumping past various obstacles, which is fine, however it may happen that you go through all obstacles just to discover you need an extra ability just to reach that sweet sweet power up, essentially removing the prize after beating the challenge.
Now, while roaming around and defeating enemies you will eventually be awarded an ability point, which can be used to improve your capabilities. In the definitive edition this system is a tad flawed: the 4th upgrade of the 3rd skill line (yes, the skill tree is made of three lines) is a bonus to an ability you unlock at the end of the game and you must get it in order to access other upgrades in that line, which is a TERRIBLE design choice (this isn't an issue in the normal version of the game). Of course there will be more upgrades for this new ability which will, obviously, be in between the ones you may want, instead of being at the end of the line. Because reasons!
You should buy this game if you don't mind frustrating games.
TLDR: a mix of super meat boy and metroid, visually stunning but frustrating gameplay and bland storyline.

Batman: Arkham Origins proudly tries to stand on the shoulders of giants, but ultimately falls short of its predecessors. Origins is the third installment of the highly praised Arkham series; a series that has shown Batman, at long last, finding success in the video game world. Rocksteady did a wonderful job making him a force to be reckoned with, as well as show his smarter, more investigate side of him. Also, up until now they did a great job of spreading out the many villains Batman has over the last few games.
Arkham Origins, unfortunately, feels like a simple copy and paste of the other games. It leans heavily on borrowed elements that made Arkham Asylum and City great. It’s sad to see since the Arkham series is arguably, not only the best of Batman video games, but maybe the best superhero licensed video games we have had. Origins simply rides the coattails of its predecessors in a cheap cash grab from WB Games.

Spec ops the line is a third person action shooter which strengths lay in its story and criticism on war.

Story
You play as Captain Walker, leading your 3 men delta squad into Dubai for a routine mission. As it turns out horrible things are happening there and you must interfere. Sadly Walker never is aware of his choices and you get bigger problems. The story takes place in a decaying Dubai which partially got buried under a desert. This now sounds like any other standard shooter, but the game makes aware of things like collateral damage and shows not only that there is no good or bad side in war, but also that there is no winner, but death.
Gameplay
Plays like any other third person shooter, nothing really special. You can sometimes use your environment to your advantage, but nothing really innovative, such as shooting a glass roof to make your enemies fall down from it. Sadly the game always tells you when you can and should do so. It lets you choose your difficulty, so it is friendly to new players. The spacebar is, as often in 3ps games, the button for everything, thus you often take cover in the wrong places, even though you wanted to sprint and take cover somewhere else.
Graphics
For 2012 it looks really good. I played it on maximum settings and it could compete with many other titles. I did not find any ugly textures, but I also did not search for them.
Multiplayer
Did not try any of those modes and I am not planning on doing so, since I do not expect too much from it.
Bugs
The only bugs I had were that 1 an enemy did not appear and thus I could not proceed, as he was counted as alive. 2, in the first two cut scenes I did not have sound. It was only the pre rendered ones, but after restarting the game without doing anything the problem solved itself, cannot guarantee that this happens to you, if you get the bug.
I do recommend it.
The game has only 5 to 10 hours main story but even without multiplayer it is worth it if not bought for full price. Right now on steam it is sold for 20€, but it is buyable on “other sites” for 3€. It is worth this, but it is not meant to be played by people who cannot handle too much criticism for their actions in a shooter. Be really sure you want to play this as I think this is 18+ for a reason (I actually didn’t notice before buying).
A social commentary on topics such as the portrayal of war and the action hero trope in modern media. One of the most gut wrenching stories told in a videogame.

There is a lot to the game of Rust, so I'm going to split this review into sections. 1: Positives. 2: Negatives. 3: Future.
Positives
- Large community with many resources available to help out new players scattered across the internet as well as a Reddit dedicated to people looking for people to play with
- Solid and well polished game play with few noticeable bugs
- Absolutely beautiful landscape
- Infinite replayability due to the fact that Rust is a multiplayer sandbox game
- Easy to understand building and crafting system
- Skill based combat system with learnable recoil in the style of Counter Strike: Global Offensive
- New progression system that ensures players can't immediately hit end-game (This helps the life of servers)
- New progression system also allows for progress to be carried over through wipes, further extending server life
- Forced server wipes every month, resetting all progress and starting back from scratch (Servers get to individually chose if they would rather wipe more frequently)
- Player interaction is frequently hilarious and completely uncontrolled by moderators (Unless by server specific rules)
- The new progression system promotes player interaction more than the last one did
- Facepunch is very good about banning exploiters as soon as they pop up
- Facepunch also listens to suggestions and other actually useful feedback
- Progress is continuous with new game updates being released every Thursday
- Difficulty is determined by other players and server specific rules
Negatives
- The community is in general rather toxic. The majority of players do not interact at all and would prefer to kill other players on sight. That said, the few that do interact make it worth it and it almost always results in a good laugh
- Rust is not fully optimized yet, so lower end computers will have trouble running the game on anything other than the lowest graphics settings
- Playing alone sucks. Some people enjoy it somehow, but I find it's not fun without at least a couple people to play with because everybody else will always outperform you. The Reddit feed I mentioned earlier is a great place to remedy that
- Rust is HARD. Modded servers make it easier for those looking for a more casual take on Rust, but in general the game is very difficult due to the kill on sight nature of most players
Future
Long story short, Rust is still in early access. It has been for years and I find that this is much more of a blessing than a curse. Many people disagree and would prefer a finished product, but the fact that it is still in early access means the developers (Facepunch) are still working on it actively and are taking feedback from their community. This leads to a better end result and a far more enjoyable experience with many new things to try out and give feedback on as development continues. There is a lot planned for the game of Rust as you can see on their website
under the roadmap tab. I urge you to try the game when it goes on sale. It's not everybody's cup of tea, but I believe I can safely say it is one of the best multiplayer survival sandbox games around.
