This game is the apex of stealth games.
Excluding the major downside that everyone seems to hate which is always online DRM, this game has so many positives that would far outweigh the negatives in the end in my opinion.
-Level Design: The levels crafted in this game are very meticulously and excellently made with the deepest details in mind, they are living, breathing pieces of the world and make you feel truly intimidated by the impossible assassinations you have to pull off.
-Assassination Creativity: Wanna make it look like an accident? Wanna eliminate a target with a bullet in their head? Or would you just rather drop a damn toilet on a target and kill them?(Legitimately in game) The possibilities are many, so many! Which brings me to my next point. But before I get to that, let's say you never heard of the Hitman franchise, let me tell you what you can do, one of the many ways to kill a target which is also what most people think of when they hear the game name Hitman, is how you can basically disguise yourself as almost anyone in the level(except women and targets..) and you can in some cases even impersonate them, for example there's this target in Sapienza seeing a mental health doctor, thing is though.. this is their first time meeting, so you go to find the doctor on the map, get to him before he gets to the target, dispose of him, take his clothes, pretend you're the doctor, sit with the target, listen to what he has to say, and kill him without anyone knowing, that's one of the MANY cases of this playstyle! That's what makes it so creative!
-Replay Value: I'm not typically the person that likes to do the same thing twice, but here, it's so very different, you basically have a mastery level in each area(also called an episode), there are 20 levels, you level up by completing challenges(creative assassinations, never detected etc..) and every time you level up you unlock things generally for all levels and/or in that specific area, let's take Paris as an example, the first time I play I start on the red carpet, but when I level up to a certain level I can start disguised as a sous-chef in the kitchen downstairs, I can also unlock new weapons that I can use there and in other levels later on, so basically I'll be able to play that level in a completely new way, especially since these levels are so huge, you'll never truly experience all of them from the first try!
-Visuals: I think the visuals look fantastic! The cloth physics are a really nice touch, the water looks really nice, I think the most beautiful level in this game is Sapienza, and i'm confident that just one look at it would be enough to convey how breathtaking the visuals in this game can be.
-No Call Of Duty style gameplay: This game doesn't let you play it like shameful displays of stealth games (Splinter Cell: Blacklist being the prime example where you can go full on combat every mission), you can't just shoot down everyone, your gun is at your disposal for assassination and small combat scenarios but if you manage to alert everyone you will NOT get out of there alive, so it's basically stealth or death, which is how it's supposed to be in a damn stealth game.
-Worth more than 60$ of content: One of the reasons this game is always online is because it's constantly adding free content, there are Elusive targets for example, a unique target with unique voicelines and story appears every 2 weeks for 168 hours, you only get one shot at killing them, if you fail, you fail forever, and if you miss them, you miss them forever, that's really cool to have! It's the most stressful thing you'll go through, but it's so worth it when you succeed! Also let's not forget the two unique free contracts added not too long ago, one of them being the bonus summer episode  set in Sapienza but is in a totally different area with so much detail put in, all for free!

-The downsides are simple, the voice acting can be better, the online DRM function is indeed annoying at times, and there are some weird bugs rarely but thankfully the game has an autosave function that is pretty well made. Also some people most notably AMD users have issues (Ironic since this game is partnered with AMD) with optimization, they tend to have frame drops, so be wary if you use AMD, don't rush to get this game, you might regret it.
To conclude I give this game a 9.5/10, might be considered high by some, but for me this is the best stealth game I have ever played, and I have played many stealth games, including Dishonored, Deus Ex and Metal Gear Solid V, but none of them emphasize stealth as much as Hitman and make you feel like a total bada$$ while doing so.

If you like hack-n-slash action games, give this one a shot. The art style is very colorful and lively. the combat system is fast and fluid and has somewhat unique strategy mechanics. The story is not award-winning but it will keep you interested and the characters are likable (Kat is my favorite character overall). Dante & Vergil do stand on their own merits: Vergil is intelligent and sneaky while Dante is brash and upfront. The level design is so awesome and I've never had so much fun platforming in a DMC game.
That being said, is this a Devil May Cry game? If you're coming here expecting that this will be EXACTLY like the old DMC, then you're out of luck. This is a fresh, new take on the franchise. Does it do things well? Well, there are flaws (no lock-on system, style score system is too easy and combat is a bit bare-bones) but it is a good enough action game for you to enjoy on a weekend. With seven difficulty modes, 21 secret missions, bloody palaceand Vergil's Downfall DLC, this game will keep you coming back for more.

Fantastic addition to the Batman Arkham series. I remember being worried that Rocksteady not developing this game would end badly, however I was gladly mistaken. It is really a spectacular addition to the series that describes one night that Black Mask puts a hit order out on Batman.
The Cons:
As you've probably read by now, the PC version here on Steam has a few bugs. Notably there is
1) Killer Croc - the first boss you have to fight can be holographic. That's right, and no it is not a plot twist. Killer Croc phases in and out of being visible rapidly making him look, as I said, holographic. However this problem is not consistent. I played through the boss level a few times and even managed to fight him once without any glitching whatsoever.
2) Cars - they can float. Every now and then look around at the cars in the game, especially police cars, as they sometimes may just be levitating off the ground.
3) End of missions - occassionally I would finish a beat down mission to interrogate someone only to find I could not interact with the person I needed to so the plot could progress. Another glitch.
Pros
1)All those glitches in the scheme of the game, while it is sad they can occur, are relatively small issues
2)The artwork is very well done and sticks to the palate we saw used in Arkham City
3)You are not playing Batman - You ARE Batman. And it looks great.
4)Troy Baker and Kevin Conroy are notably excellent voice actors in a top-notch voice acting ensemble
5)Same control scheme, makes it a great way to wait until the final Batman game is finished and released
In the end, if you are a Batman fan and enjoyed Arkham City you will find great enjoyment here. Make it through Killer Croc (albeit painfully if he glitches) and you are in for a ride. Plus waiting until a Steam Sale makes the few glitches much more tolerable.

Without spoiling anything first, if you haven't played this game, do so. Play it in one sitting, only takes 4-7 hours max, don't bother with high difficulty, the story is better than the gameplay, and you better have the audio on/not be listening to other things. It's worth your time.
Now all that being said, if you need to know more, this is a decent cover based third person shooter, with one of the most intense stories I've seen in a shooter. You're sent to find out what happened to the lost 33rd Army division who was sent to rescue the citizens of Dubai after a major sandstorm destroyed the city, and they never reported back. It's a descent into the madness that exists in the city after it's cut off from the world, and how the psyche handles it. The gameplay is nothing special, and turning up the difficulty just makes it more drawn out than fun as the enemies become bullet sponges, so just turn that down and play to "enjoy" the story.  You WILL want to YouTube some scenes later as there are many instances of multiple choices you could make and you'll want to see what you could have chosen instead.

Hitman is the sequel to the heavily criticize Hitman: Absolution. Fans of the series constantly ripped on Absolution due to it linear gameplay and lack of replayability. Although at first look Hitman with it episodic release may appear to be another cash grab by Square Enix, I was gladly mistaken. The episodes created by IO Interactive was both massive and filled with life. Each mission will begin with Agent 47 briefed of his target and thrown into a interactive sandbox where the player can organically learn about each target either through eavesdropping on the NPC or stalking the target across the map. After each successful assasination Hitman push us to eliminate the target again in different ways. Every consequective playthrough on the assasination missions we learn new information about our target. This really hit home for me during the Sapienza mission, where I disguised myself as a shrink for one of the target. The emotion I felt after hearing about our target dirty laundry actually made me pity him.

This is not the game you expect it to be.
I should start by saying I normally never would buy a game such as this because it's simply not my style of game. I moved away from this play style back when I was a pre-teen.
My first impressions were that this game was not worth the full price and that it was probably not even that good since it was 2D and it probably lacked on what was needed to make it successfull (at least to me), "substance". So I figured "What the hell. It's half off. Why not?" Best decision I have made buying a video game.
Never in my life have I experienced something like Ori and the Blind Forest for a video game. Never has something caused this many tears in such a short time. The amount of emotional toil that this game can play on you  is astounding. This game will have you hooked from start to finish.
Within the first 3 minutes of starting the game I was crying. "Boss" encounters were no exception. For some reason I would just start crying as well. The mix of powerful music with this jaw dropping atmosphere and this pull you get during it all. When you accomplish these big events you feel it. You really feel it.
The combat and how abilities worked were well done. It always felt that when you picked up a new ability you were able to incorporate it into your arsenal of abilities before you gained anymore. You always get to start feeling comfortable with your new found power before you have to put them to test.
Probably one of the biggest things I enjoyed was how the characters were portrayed. Now I don't want to spoil anything so I will only say this. These characters are far more complicated then they appear. Lines feel blurred and in the end you may be standing on the fence.
I've never written a review before. I just feel that this game is something everyone should experience. You may not enjoy it as a child or a teen, but I feel if you are able to grab that part inside of you this game will take you on a journey that you won't forget anytime soon.

This is not game. It's a short story or possibly even a short film. Either way it isn't a game. You're a girl, Nina, and you go to a bar because your friend told you to. Your friend is late and you get sexually assaulted. Then it ends. The player has no agency or choice in anything. That could possibly be the point though, as in the lack of mechanic is there to mirror the lack of choice the character has as well. The feeling of helplessness is mirrored in the fact as a player you cannot help her. But, the problem is, you don't really care about the character. For a short story, short film, art game, whatever this is where the entire point is the story you should have to care about the characters. This game has no back story, no character building, no world building. Nothing. The most you really learn about Nina is she drinks long island ice teas. I think the game relies on the fact you will feel bad because it's a true story. To be fair, I did feel bad through the assault but that has nothing to do with the game. I'm just a human being with empathy and sympathy and I will feel bad for someone who is assaulted. But this game did not truely shape my feelings. Thinking about it, this game relies solely on that ending scene of the assault. Without it the game is nothing. Without those outside feelings, the game has absolutely nothing.
I do not recomend this game. If it sounds interesting to you, then maybe. The game is 5 minutes long, shorter if you're a fast reader, but it holds no substance. I am a person who usually enjoys slow empty short stories where maybe one thing happens and nothing much. In other words, I tend to love vignettes, but this game is just not a well written one. It's just not worth it.

So I have nothing with trucks, car or engines really. I love how people can spend hours fine tuning their high detail modded trucks, but that's not me. What I do get out of Euro Truck Simulator is some relaxed driving time; plug in a steering wheel, drive a bit, enjoy some scenery and clear out my head.
As a game (mechanics wise), this one might be a bit weak in middle to long term. You drive, make money, repeat, buy a truck, hire a driver, buy a garage and repeat some more. This process speeds up as you gather more trucks, personnel and garages since they will bring in income too. There is no real long term goal.
However, in my opinion, that's not the point. If you enjoy an occasional drive (and I do feel this is the minimum requirement for getting enough out), this game will bring you a nice stress free experience.
As a final note, a steering wheel is not required and driving with mouse + keyboard or controller is still fairly enjoyable. I must admit getting a wheel quite soon however, as I feel the experience was incomplete without it. This investment might mean additional costs to factor in.

This game is really dark, and deals with some very controversial topics. But this is what makes the campaign a real experience. Some examples without spoiling anything are depictions of child soldiers (only in cutscenes, you don't kill any), gruesome torture scenes, and some gibs. gibbing is when you use a weapon to make someone's limbs come off. Usually the more high power weapons such as shotguns, snipers and explosives. This includes everything from arms, legs, feet, and very rarely (happened once for me after 3 or 4 play throughs) decapitation. Luckily, most of these effects can be turned off, as the game allows you to turn off "graphic content". This includes removing gibs, the gore from torture scenes, censoring swearing, and censoring brutal violence in cutscenes. Of course, having graphic content disabled will not remove any parts important to the story, but will tone back anything not particularly importamt. For example the first mission of the game starts as you attempt to save a soldier in a burning humvee. With graphic content enabled, you can see him being burned alive inside as you try to rescue him. With graphic content disabled, you still try to break the glass, but you cannot see anyone inside the humvee.
Really, the dark atmosphere is what makes this game great

I have to say that when I first played this game I found it so boring and laborious that I tossed it aside after about 2 hours to go play some microsoft Spider Solitaire for some thrills.  With so many other reviews being positive though and a great set of promo trailers I figured that there must be something to it if I gave it a second chance, damn am I glad I did!  The game does start off very slowly and quite boring, that is still my opinion, but after a few hours, once you reach Sanctuary it just gets better...and better...and better.  From Sanctuary the game really takes off with an ever expanding collection of quirky, kinky, sick and generally hillarious characters.
I have now played the entire game through once as well as most of the challenges and side-missions.  I am now about half way through playing the game for a second time as well as having since purchased several of the add-on head-hunter missions and ultimate vault hunters upgrade 2.
If I had to make any criticisms they would be the lack of a basic guide to how the backpack works, how level-ups and badass ranks are worked etc.  I think I reached level 7 or something before I figured out how to use them, as for customizations, about a quarter of the way through my second game(but since it is mostly first person whats the point), I also did not understand a few other things but perhaps I am just slow.  By far though, the biggest major dissapointment I could pick with Borderlands 2 is that, despite what the promo-trailers and Claptrap might suggest, there is not even a single moment of "Wang Chung" played anywhere throughout the game.
On the up-side though, if I had to give any credit to the designers...ermmm, absolutely friggin everything!!!  This game is absolutely awesome, the dark humour is hillariously sick and brings into question the very state of their mental health, I just love it.  Going to buy the Pre-Sequel very soon.
Overall advice, if you are pondering buying this game, ponder no more, just buy it, after a few hours you will not regret it at all.  To those who have complained that Borderlands 2 is to hard, if you want something simple then stick to "noughts and crosses", games are meant to be challenging rather than spoonfeeders.
I rate it as 9.8/10.

Without spoiling anything first, if you haven't played this game, do so. Play it in one sitting, only takes 4-7 hours max, don't bother with high difficulty, the story is better than the gameplay, and you better have the audio on/not be listening to other things. It's worth your time.
Now all that being said, if you need to know more, this is a decent cover based third person shooter, with one of the most intense stories I've seen in a shooter. You're sent to find out what happened to the lost 33rd Army division who was sent to rescue the citizens of Dubai after a major sandstorm destroyed the city, and they never reported back. It's a descent into the madness that exists in the city after it's cut off from the world, and how the psyche handles it. The gameplay is nothing special, and turning up the difficulty just makes it more drawn out than fun as the enemies become bullet sponges, so just turn that down and play to "enjoy" the story.  You WILL want to YouTube some scenes later as there are many instances of multiple choices you could make and you'll want to see what you could have chosen instead.
8/10

Introduction:
The game takes place in an post post-apocalyptic Dubai, but what happens in the game's story rings true to every war that ever took place. Futhermore, I am sure that if a war veteran would play this game, it would be likely to trigger PTSD, due to the nature of imagery and feel that it gives.
Pros:
-Really good, balanced and haunting story

The game ends up being a great anti-war game that focuses on the atrocities that man is able to commit when pushed beyond limit, it's being held back a bit by the gameplay, which feels poorly ported. Nevertheless, I still highly recommend getting this game.

Play this game. But be warned it..will..change you. And, it will hurt. But perhaps you will learn something about yourself by doing so. I strongly advise you to prepare youself for some very intense tscenes.

Surprisingly good. Spec Ops: The Line is not just another shooter set in the modern day. It's very story-focused, putting you into the shoes of Captain Walker and his squadmates, and making you live through the harrowing events they had to face when deployed in war-torn Dubai.
The game has a very cinematic feel to it. The scenes build up gradually to big climaxes, and the squadmates discussing what's going on and arguing with one another the entire time, making them seem like real people and not just mindless NPCs. In addition, the game presents you with some moral choices at times, making you think twice on your decisions and putting you in situations where neither choice can be considered good. Without giving away any spoilers, the game concludes on a mindblowing ending, or more precisely - endings, whilst leaving some ambiguity behind to let the players interpret the rest. I would highly suggest to play the game to the end and then to check the Youtube videos to see all the endings and their interpretations.
Story aside, the gameplay is pretty fun as well. The combat is fun and for the most part consists of your typical third-person cover-based gunfights. There is some variety in the environments where you fight, ranging from desert outposts to insides of malls and other semi-broken buildings, as well as rooftops. This in turn presents some interesting challenges from time to time, such as defence sections and the like. It could get a bit repetitive, however, and some of the bigger gunfights do feel a bit messy at times. Additionally, the squadmates and the enemies wear similar-coloured uniforms, so it's very easy to mistake a fellow ally for an enemy during a heated combat. The crosshairs of some weapons turn red when on the enemy, but this isn't the case for all weapons, so it's easy to accidentally hurt your allies.
Overall I've enjoyed my time with this game. Although the combat started to get repetitive and a bit frustrating towards the end, the story makes it well worth playing the game through from start to finish. Recommended.

I like it a lot. Initially, I wanted a game that simulated traffic laws that would be adhered to, accompanied with nice graphics. This game excellently involves you with speed limits, turn signals, traffic signals, etc. , and tacks on fines for breaking them.
Of course, I was also pleasantly engaged with the game's experience system, economy, and business management.
Starting off small, you can take on cheap jobs across Europe without your own truck, borrowing a company's instead. Once you've done enough jobs, and or taken loans from the bank, you can purchase your own truck from a variety of real-life companies with their own specific stats for your style. The truck has to be maintained by being fuelled and repaired when it gets damaged. Additionally, there are customizable features including interior decorations and exterior paint jobs. Your character will be fatigued, requiring you to sleep, and will gain experience throughout successful deliveries. Levelling up offers new skills which aid you with passive bonuses (such as fuel consumption) and additional revenue with special cargo (fragile, explosive, high-value, etc.). I enjoy this level of detail which makes me WANT to progress and improve my character's abilities and truck.
After garnering enough cash to expand your business, you can upgrade & build new garages, hire employees with varying skillsets (which include the skills available to you), provide them their own trucks, and watch as your empire expands all across the country and continent. Of course, you don't have to, but it adds another layer of depth to the game that is nice for those who like to micromanage.
It's a nice way to pass the time driving (aimlessly or for a job) while listening to the radio, watching the pleasant countryside scenery, and conquering the continent with your trucks.

From the same people who brought you a game about being an eleven year old girl making her dolls have sex comes a non-interactive non-game that literally takes less than three minutes to "play" and consists of a series of images with some text. In other words, a comic book. Well, actually, it is more like a comic strip. Those creepy religious chick tracts things you find sometimes at a bus stop have more content and are just as interactive (you have to turn the page). Actually, the game's store page has more content than the actual game.
This isn't a "choose your own adventure" of any kind. It is not interactive fiction. It is a linear click-through that tells you the story of a girl who goes to a party and is groped on the stoop on her way into the party, about three seconds after saying "hi" to a guy. That's it.
On the positive side, this does have *slightly* more content than one of those tiny little comic strips that come in a five-cent stick of Bazooka Bubblegum.
I came to this title, intending to give it a fair shake and a possibly positive review because the author was mentioned as complaining about how Steam is unfair to developers like her, because they require you to play a game for five minutes before leaving a review and
. I figured she was exaggerating about how short her title was, but was happy to give it a try and leave one of those desired reviews that were mentioned. I like to support indie devs and hear more voices in gaming, so why not?
Unfortunately, I discovered that this wasn't a game and it really was only a couple minutes long. I don't really understand why it is on Steam. Not because I'm someone who rails against walking-simulators or "interactive experiences". I believe that not everything that is created with game tools has to be a "game" and while I was not a fan of Gone Home, I really liked Dear Esther, 3am, Homesick, and numerous others. However, this was not an "interactive experience" created by game tools. It is just a very short web-comic. It would be more fitting as a Tumblr, Reddit, or DeviantArt post than in a game store.
It is too brief to manage evoking meaningful empathy or response from the viewer. You don't know the characters, anything about them, or care about anything that happens to them. The incident that occurs is brief and obviously nobody condones someone being forcibly groped, but a groping in and of itself doesn't elevate the rest of the content to something you care about any more than a two minute store that starts with "a guy walks across the street and then is hit by a car and dies" does. Sure, death sucks, but . . . we don't care about this particular faceless empty vessel of a character.
It all literally just hinges on a groping to carry it and force peopel to fell compelled to give it more meaning than it deserves, so as not to be the social outcast that isn't basking this outstanding artistic impression in the halo of light that it wants to deserve.
Ultimately, this just feels like some high school kid was tasked with having to create a game and the kid couldn't really be bothered, so they slapped together a few pictures and called it a "game" and submitted it in hopes of achieving the absolute minimum effort required by their teacher.
It seems this is common for this group of indies, though. Go see the MS Paint "game" titled "How do you do it?", about an eleven year old girl trying to figure out sex by mashing her dolls together. Yeah, it has about as much content as Freshman Year. Another title that just belonged in a high school kid's portfolio and not, you know, experienced by the rest of the world. Oh, that game is also on Steam, because Steam will allow literally anything.
Oh, but it's "autobiographical" (as they keep promoting about both of these games), so that somehow excuses the lack of . . . everything.
Sorry I couldn't offer a more positive review. I came here really expecting to be able to do so. I just never imagined this could be as trivial, inane, and worthless as it actually was. I'm sorry the person had a bad experience in real life, but that doesn't have anything to do with the poor quality of this title. Perhaps as much time should have been put into the content of the "game" as has been put into complaining about people not liking it and leaving negative reviews.

Nina's games aren't for everyone, and they don't have to be. This is a story, a short vignette, and a brief but affecting experience. You won't be jumping or shooting or solving puzzles. If you're looking exclusively for something like that, this won't be your kind of thing.
If you enjoy very human stories that express real life experiences, anxieties, and fears in a very honest way, you should give this game a go.
Nina's games tend to express an emotional vulnerability which is rare in any medium, and rarer still in the world of games -- even considering the indie world. Engage with her games while keeping that in mind and you may find yourself surprised at the emotional resonance she's able to evoke.
Some other reviewers have complained about the lack of actual branching despite the illusion of choice. These reviewers have missed an important point. It's natural for survivors of sexual assault to wonder if there's something they could have done differently to avoid the situaton -- maybe if they waited at the apartment longer, or took a different route, etc. The lack of branching here isn't a product of laziness, it's an intentional design decision which plays into the very anxieties the story expresses.
And for the reviewers spewing all the bile: it's not like you paid for it anyway, so what's with all the hate? You said it yourself, it only took a few minutes. So get over yourselves, just because you didn't like it doesn't make it worthless.

Freshman year is a powerful, emotional game that explores the unfortunately all-too-common experience of sexual assualt. Excellent design, writing, artwork, and music.

"Freshman Year is a vignette game about an ordinary night in the life a college freshman named Nina."
This describes the game to a T. It's a short, interactive story that allows the player to experience what the designer intended in a more visceral way than simply watching an animation or reading a description of the event. The idea here, at least to me, is to demonstrate that women ultimately face the threat of abuse wherever they go, and that even those people who have to deal with that threat every day can brush it off in unsettling ways that just perpetuate our problematic system.
When you finish, the events are likely to sit with you a while. It's really something that deserves unpacking. The fact that the choices make very slight changes to the text you see and the way events unfold, but that the story still plays out in essentially the same way, with exactly the same ending, reinforces the fact that these kinds of abuses are completely out of the hands of the people they're committed against, and changes to one's own behavior have very little impact on when and how things like this happen.
Recommended, everyone should play through it at least once.

Borderlands 2 is an FPS/RPG hybrid with cel-shaded graphics. Taking place on the planet of Pandora (not the one from Avatar), you play as 1 of 4 classes (6 if you have the appropriate DLC) who comes to Pandora as a Vault Hunter, hoping to find riches and glory. Opposing you is Handsome Jack, ruler of the planet, and a sadistic, self-absorbed ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who taunts you from beginning to end. As you go through the game, you can find guns of 6 different types, as well as grenades. You'll also gradually unlock 2 extra weapon slots. There are also Shields, Relics, Grenade Mods, and Class Mods. Making your way to the central hub of Sanctuary, you'll meet a variety of memorable characters like Lilith (who has her own cult following), the Dr. Nick-esque Dr. Zed, and of course, the voluptous Moxxi. There's also Claptrap, who helps you at the beginning of the game, but after you get to Sanctuary, he stays in a corner except for a few sidequests while you focus on everyone else.
The game feels like an adventure. Felt like you where going somewhere on the Southern Shelf? That's just the tip of the iceberg. Like RPGs, you'll constantly be replacing guns that are dropped by enemies and found in armories. Ammo isn't all that hard to find, contained in chests, and more importantly, can be bought at Ammo Dump vending machines. Money is mostly spent on ammo, and if you die, respawning. As a result, you won't be needing money much. I still wound up with over $40,000 at the end of the game (and that's also with tipping Moxxi $10,000 for the Sugar Daddy achievement). What you will need is the precious purple Eridium, which increases your max capacity on ammo (don't waste it on the safe).
Also unique is the "Fight For Your Life" mechanic. When you run out of health, the world turns black-and-white, you move more slowly, and you can't use zoom or grenades. Kill an enemy to gain Second Wind, then fall back and recharge. This is also where multiplayer comes in. Up to 4 people can play, and when someone is Fighting For Their Life, another player can Revive them, allowing them to stay in the field longer. When you're all done for the day, you can use various Fast Travel points to warp back to Sanctuary, as well as anywhere else in the world that you unlocked a Fast Travel point.
The most disappointing feature is the vehicles. There are only two types, one is a two-seater, the other is a 4-seater. Granted, you're not going to use a vehicle in every zone, but it feels like unfulfilled potential.
Overall, Borderlands 2 is a great game with a memorable world and characters, and I do want to finish up the sidequests and DLC. Maybe I'll get around to playing Tales From The Borderlands and the Pre-Sequel.

TL;DR: Great story, feels like Arkham City but plagued with inconsistent controls and game-breaking bugs.
First off I should mention that I own and *love* the first 2 Batman Arkham games that Rocksteady developped but this one, not so much.
Let's start with the good stuff: the game's story. The story feels like a genuine Batman creation with its usual assortment of strange and compelling villains, of which there are quite a few and they're all wonderfully voiced and gorgeously animated. The premise of the story is itself enough to draw interest as the new villain of the game and of the Batman universe, Black Mask, orders a hit on Batman and a large number of would-be and professional assassins flock to Gotham to take the Bat out. The rogue's gallery is incredible, ranging from favourites such as Bane, Lady Shiva, Killer Croc and Deathstroke to newcommers like Copperhead and all of the encounters are sufficiently awesome with excellent boss fights (although I was disappointed with how easily Deathstroke was dealt with in comparison to say, Bane).
Another great aspect of the game are the murder mysteries and investigations that you solve through an impressive use of detective vision as you re-create the crime scenes using different angles, following trails, examining forensic evidence, etc. This is one area where I feel that WB Games has improved upon compared to Arkham Asylum and Arkham City as the manner in which the data is extrapolated and the murders solved is more complex & convincing. Well done WB Games, well done.
And that's where the good stuff ends. From this point onwards things start to fall apart, starting with the glitchy combat controls where you might find yourself pressing counter and nothing happens to the buggy and immersion-breaking environment where you'll see high ledges that you'll be unable to land upon even though they look exactly like any other surface that Batman routinely grabs and walks across. Arkham City did this better with its walls and gunner watch towers but here it just feels like poor game design.
But the worst of it all as others here have experienced and mentioned in their reviews are the game-breaking bugs. At about 55% through the game I reached a point where the game bugged out on me and I was falling endlessly through a void. This wouldn't be so bad if there was an option to have more than 1 saved game & your progress didn't get automatically saved, leaving you stuck with no option but to start from the very begining and hope you don't get the bug again. This is a notorious Arkham Origins game bug that obviously still hasn't been fixed to this day despite half-hearted attempts at patches which is simply unacceptable.
Due to this I have been unable to complete the game as I refuse to re-start from the begining with no guarantee that this won't happen again. It's a shame as I genuinely enjoyed the story but I guess I'll just youtube the cutscenes instead.
I'll never buy any of your games again, WB Games.

Although Arkham Origins is not as high-quality or polished as Asylum and City, it has some surprisingly fun elements that make it worth it. You get to play as Deathstroke during the challenge maps, which are pretty well-made (but glitchy), and I actually found the multiplayer quite fun. For new Arkham players, get this and do not run away from the series if you think this is glitchy. APB on the surface is an amazing game. Being able to play the role of a vigilate cop or a hardened criminal is enticing, and the fully customizable characters, cars, and tattoos are awesome features to boot. However, when you download the game and play it for a day or two, you quickly realize that the grandeour of what was promised is simply just not delivered...
While true the custimization is a very developed feature, the actual gameplay is less than desirable. Essentially missions are the same across the board, either defend somthing, or attack and maybe shuttle a car or an object (cocaine, evidence, ect...) to a specified area. During that time, it's a slugfest between the players who have no sense of cooperation, or are just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s in general. More on that later though
The guns in APB serve genaric roles, short, medium, or long range with the option of sidearms to compensate for weaknesses. The guns are generally ok, but the ones bought from the ARMA shop (paid with real cash) offer significant advantages to the vanilla guns, such as longer range, higher ammo capacity, and faster rate of fire. Now, the vanilla guns have the capacity to rival these weapons, but it takes an incredible amount of experience with the gun of your choice (SMG, Assualt Rifle ect...) to gain access to the mods that will alter the weapon.
So it can be argued that this game isn't pay to win because the players who don't pay can EVENTUALLY rival the people who do pay, there is a very noticable difference in power, and you'll see it too. The weapon I most often see against me is the "Whisper" submachine gun varient. It is designed to hide muzzle flash and noise while also boosting range at a negligible difference in stopping power. This weapon is only available with real money, and while you can mod a submachine gun to get some benefit, the silencer is exclusive to the "Whisper". This gives a player an incredible advantage over other players who dont want to pay. This is just one example though, there are multiple weapons on the ARMA market that offer similar exclusive features not found anywhere in the vanilla game. It makes going against these players incredibly frustrating to go against, and unless you have significant skill and willpower, odds are they are going to kill you repeatedly.
Besides unfair weapons, the playerbase in APB is terrible, and doing missions is nigh impossible, ESPECIALLY IF YOU ARE NEW. Players, who are on your team, will kill you if they feel you are a noob or are slowing them down, they either think its funny to pick on you, or they just are really that upset at you. They will just kick you in most cases (Somtimes after killing you) without a second thought. If you get into one of their precious modded vehicles (to get a ride to an objective for example), they will either leave and go spawn their car and leave without you, get out of their car and demand you leave, (surprise!) just kick you from the mission, or a combination of all three. While it can't be applied to all players, I've met a few people who were great to work with, the majority of the community are in cliques and can be quite mean to new players or lone wolves, and I've seen it happen. Somtimes it even gets to the point where it could be considered cyber bullying, and I'm not joking or exagerating about that.
All in all, APB is a title that I wanted to be a good game. It just wasn't there though, and I feel now my time has been wasted. I suggest you avoid this game and spend your time and money elsewhere.

ah, Call of Duty Black Ops II. back when people ran on the ground, people dived instead of sliding (which in my opinion is cooler than sliding), and the future setting actually used stuff that seemed futuristic instead of sci-fi fapping material.
if someone out there is considering to buy this game 4 years after it's release (and counting), here's a general rundown of the game.
CAMPAIGN:
there's two different setting here, the past and the future. in the past you hunt down a terrorist called Menendez who has info on some stuff. in the future, you hunt down Menendez who has turned into a terrorist and is planning to throw the world into chaos using something called Celerium. basically Celerium makes your toaster go crazy.
MULTIPLAYER:
the main part of the Call of Duty franchise is the multiplayer, and this is (or was) the most fun multiplayer there is. you can pick from a variety of weapons, from pistols, to SMGs to a ♥♥♥♥ing riot shield that you can plant into the ground which gives you some cover to hide behind. but there's no real point in playing this, since there's only a couple of thousand players still online when i last checked.
ZOMBIES:
do yourself a favor and buy the last DLC for this game, which contains the map Origins. it's by far the best Zombies map in this game. if you don't want that, here's a little rundown of what's going on.
the world has been destroyed, it's full of zombies, and you are a part of a small group of survivors consisting of a nerd, a hobo, a teacher and boobs. the teacher has eaten zombie flesh, which grants him the ability to talk to a german called Richtofen, who controls the zombies on the moon. don't ask me why. they roam the planet to do stuff Richtofen tells the teacher, and the others just go on with it.
also at some point you play as some mobsters in Alcatraz where zombies also are, but they're from hell, and there's a flaming wolf eating zombies that grants you an indian tomahawk.
so yeah. that's Black Ops II in a nutshell. if you really want to know what's going on, just look up a video on Youtube.

I don't think I ever saw a flash game occupy a whooping 127MB of hard drive space.  Anyway, you spend all of those two minutes taking Nina to a bar to meet her friend.  While she's waiting outside, a dude starts trying to make out with her.  Then her friend shows up and drags her into the bar.  The end.
1/10

No a game in as much as it is a storybook. The choices you make don't really matter, but that's the point isn't it? Effective in its execution, and the art style and music fit the message perfectly.  It has a very "national film board" kind of feel to it which is both classic and disconcerting.
It's not long, and lacks something in closure (again, that's the point, isn't it?) I can't say I enjoyed it, exactly, but I thought it was very good.

This is a linear short story hidden under the perception of clicking on "choices". None of the choices impact the story.
However, it's important to note that the story is autobiographical.  So is it fair to expect the maker to change a highly emotional, true experience?  I don't think so.  We were invited to share in her story, and to explore the concepts of "what ifs" is not healthy.  Instead, this acts more like a cautionary tale on the reliability of friends and the reflection of decisions once made.
I would have liked to see more depth to the story and the characters.  I think it would make a great introduction to a longer vignette about how Nina learns to be assertive or more independent.
Recommended because it is worth the time it takes to play.

This is an autobiographical visual short story, rather than a game.  There are no choices to be made, other than marginally different dialogues that don't change the events of the story.  It's very short, but it's also free.  It tells an unsettling story involving sexual misconduct, so if that upsets you, be warned.
The art style goes well with the creepy music and strange pacing.  The effect of the main character always looking toward her phone during uncomfortable scenes struck me as particularly genuine.  How often do we look towards distraction while in potentially embarrassing situations.  The story is told fairly realistically in its portrayal of a awkward inexperienced girl unable to identify the severity of the danger in a particular social situation.  After an disturbing encounter, she is at a loss on how to handle it.
The ending could use work.  It was sudden and offered no closure, but I think this was deliberate.  In real life there would be no closure.  People would continue on as they always did, and the girl would still be at a loss for what to do.  Those around her would take their cues from her and not react in outrage, since she was too stunned to show outrage.  It's interesting how much a criminal can get away with if they just smile and pretend they're doing nothing wrong.  I'm pretty sure that's what happened here, and it was only with reflection that Nina realized how terrible that situation was and how much worse it could have gotten.
To the writer/developer:  Even if this is based on true events, for the purposes of relating the story to others, it would have been a good idea to include some kind of ending text.  All it really needed was a paragraph or two summing up the end of their evening and how life just continued on after that night, regardless of what happened or what almost happened.

What you'd expect from a worthy Mad Max game.
- Open world post-apocalyptic scenario which blends exploration, car combat and melee combat? check
- Car combat with amazing explosions and deaths? check
- The most satisfying melee combat I've ever seen in a game with grapples, wall executions and counters? check
- Lots of customization and upgrades for Max, his cars and strongolds? check
- Hundreds of unlocks and collectibles? check
- 70s muscle car goodness? check
- Lots of action and destruction? check
- People eating maggots and dog food to survive? check
- Guns and bullets being scarce but a single shot fired can be a game changer on an uphill battle? check
- Game being so well optimized that it runs at 4k60 ultra on a GTX 1060? check
- Max being as badass as they come? check
Of course the game has its cons:
- Steering control gets stuck and unresponsive at times, which can lead you crashing into a canyon for a quick demise, which can be frustrating.
- Aiming can be quite frustrating, and slowing down time doesn't help if the game slows down your aim in an attemp to assist you.
- Game still has many bugs as of November 2017.
All and all for its current price it's a definitive steal. This is the Mad Max game I've always dreamed about.
I highly recommend it unless you're tired of open world games.

I loved Arkham Asylum and City, but hadn't realised when I got this one that it had been offloaded to a different development team. I got maybe half way through the story and I was wondering why I really wasn't enjoying this one as much as the previous ones (which I just couldn't stop playing).... So then I looked it up and it all became clear. I wish there was a meh rating between thumbs up and thumbs down because it isn't really bad enough for a thumbs down but it doesn't really merit a thumbs up...
So, basically it's a perfectly good game it's just not nearly as good as the ones that came before it. The storyline is just rather mangled - it has some good ideas and some really stunning moments, but in general they have recycled everything directly from the other two games and in the case of the gadgets which were discovered as the story progressed in the other two, suddenly already having them all in a prequel seems a little ...weird. They didn't even try to make them slightly more clunky or restrricted or anything...
The combat also feels less fluid and has a tendancy to screw up if one of the people in the group needs to be interrogated (which unfortunately is often). Game mechanisms that you grow to rely on such as the ability to slide into a grate will suddenly cease working in certain areas. Bugs in the game mean that you may find uninterrogatable people who impede your progress due to them having information you need (or in one case grapple points decided to not appear leading to having to do a rather tricky run/jump/scrabble on a previously easily climbable wall).
The skills/levelling system includes challenges in each of the four main categories - hitting things, geography aka flying/hitting stuff in certain places, hitting things while in a stealth type situation and of course collecting stuff. These have to be completed sequentially and due to the low number of predator encounters that are actually useful for some of these it's possible to get half way through the game and be unable to continue progressing one section because there are no longer the required areas available. Easily solved if you could complete them in any order or if the challenges counted...but they didn't. So man up and play through the whole game again to get them?
Whilst in the City open world there were the odd bits you couldn't climb it was usually obvious why. In this game you are surrounded by obviously climbable buildings that for some reason you cannot climb. For no reason. Not even because they serve some plot point. Just random normal buildings with obvious things you should be able to grapple onto ...and you can't. Occasionally they stick collectibles up there but mostly it just seems to restrict your freedom in an irritating way for no apparent reason.
The collectibles are ...meh. There are no really interesting mechanics. There really doesn't feel like much incentive to be honest. I really wanted to solve all the Riddler's puzzles before, but now... it feels like he doesn't really care so why should I? I still haven't finished the invisible collectibles like the anarchy signs but far from feeling like I want to hunt them down, I'm wondering whether or not to bother.
Its saving grace for me has been the theme of everything going to hell at Christmas time (the game begins on Christmas Eve). Christmas is always a time of huge stress for me since I have to organise it, and this year really has been a kicker so far, going above and beyond in its efforts to destroy what little Christmas spirit I have left. I find it vaguely reassuring that at least Batman's been having a worse time of it than me and nobody tries to get him to be jolly about it...

As far as achievements go, Quadrant M4 is one of the weirdest games I've played.
There are 1544 achievements.
You can get the whole lot of them in a few minutes, even if you don't move from the starting point.
It took me 4 minutes to get achievements 1 to 22.
At first I was shooting at passing asteroids, testing the different weapons, and trying to figure out how the game works, and then I noticed that the achievements were racking up even when I wasn't doing anything. What the?
That's right, you get achievements in this game just by doing nothing.
Perhaps they're special achievements for idling?
After all, doing nothing is a highly specialised technique - I've been working on that ability for years now, devoting at least 6-8 hours every night to that particular skill-set.
By the way, there is no achievement 21 or 23, as it looks like the developer couldn't even be bothered to number the achievements properly; in fact, after achievement 25 the rest aren't even numbered at all.
So, the first few achievements were dead easy.
Then I read a post which said you just need to restart the game to get the rest - so I restarted the game and almost instantly got every other achievement in the same minute (possibly in the same second, as it all seemed to happen at once).
That's just ridiculous, getting 1544 achievements for doing nothing; even worse, getting 1523 of them simultaneously.
Maybe it's all very nice if you are purely an achievement hunter; but, seriously, that's not what games are about - or, at least, it shouldn't be.

I originally purchased this game around the time that the sequel - Euro Truck Simulator 2 - was getting rave reviews. So why not buy the sequel? Because it was priced ten times more and - reviews aside - it seemed doubtful I would enjoy a game where I tediously drove a truck down highways avoiding traffic hauling cargo. At least, I thought,  the first game would give me an idea if I could even stomach the genre. And if it did, well only then would I consider paying the price for the sequel.
I was surprised out how engaging this game was. Perhaps because it stood in such stark contrast to all my other driving games (the Need For Speed series, Burnout Paradise, and similar), but there was something very relaxing  and enjoyable about driving between the lanes, making a point not to speed (much) and slam into other cars. It was almost zenlike. The graphics might not be particularly impressive but they got the point across, and the AI of the other cars was pleasantly non-aggressive. Figuring out the best routes to take and what cargos to deliver was not particularly challenging but it was relaxing, and a welcome change from the ordinary.
Sadly, that's not enough to sustain the game, at least not for me. Having advanced three tiers and played over twenty hours, the lack of variety is increasingly noticeable. I actually dislike most of the action (adventure) games like God Of War and Devil May Cry. They're usually all about the combat, which becomes a boring aspect for me a few hours into the game. And yes, they have great visuals most of the times, but visuals isn't a key aspect for me. Then again; they do help to pull the player into the game world.
Anyway, DmC managed to surprise me because of it's environments, fluent combat and, maybe even more important for me; short campaign. You read correctly, a short campaign. It will take a player somewhere between 7,5-12 hours to fully complete one playthrough, which is a decent length and for me long enough to not become boring or overstay its welcome.
The new Dante starts off as an annoying, run-of-the-mill character. But along the way I started caring for him. He grew more mature it seemed.
Dante will start the game with some basic weaponry and will get new moves and weapons until late in the game, which keeps the combat fresh. Obviously, all weapons and moves can be upgraded. And there really are some amazing moves in there. Using a controller I was able to pull off some of the hardest combos. I'll admit, there was some button mashing involved, but most of the times I actually knew what I was doing.
The environments steal the show though. Rarely have I seen environments this brilliant. The TV show (including boss fight) and nightclub levels are some of the best levels I've ever seen in a game. DmC uses a variety of bright colors, while still having a certain gothic feel to it. It's exceptional.
You can tell they put some real love into the PC version since it will never dip below 60FPS. On Ultra settings things look (mostly) sharp and seeing the game in motion is a real treat, especially during the acrobatic (non-)combat sequences.
The voice acting is top notch, but, unfortunately, the story is a bit on the light side.
Time to wrap things up: I had a great time with this game and I would gladly recommend it to all serious gamers out there.

Prison Architect is a game that, after a short learning period, I have come to really enjoy. It isn't perfect by any means, and there is a lot of room for improvement. Contructing intricate building can be cumbersome and frustrating. Keeping your prisoners from rioting can be stressful. I can say in full confidence that the enjoyable aspects of prisoner architect far outweigh the drawbacks. I am still relatively new to the game, and I am eager to learn parts of the game that I haven't yet experienced. I've had a chance to check out some community prisons and it is truly incredible what you can build in this game!
In Prison Architect, you play as an omnipotent being. You have the power to plan your prison, hire staff, and allocate prisoners to a living space. At first, you will likely build a quaint holding cell, surrounded by supplemental facilities. Over time, you will have the opportunity to build intricate cell blocks, classrooms, chapels, visitation centers, parole offices, canteens, administrative buildings, and much, much more. Building your prison is where the fun begins.
The game really takes off when it comes to managing your prison. Do you want to run a luxury prison or do you want to rule with an iron fist? Do you want to build a resort or a Gulag? Are you okay with daily bathroom shankings, or do you want all your prisoners and staff to be as safe as possible? I have found that in my earlier stages, I was stressing to keep my prisoners happy. This caused me to indulge my inmates with luxurious prison cells, fully equipped with personal showers and computer desks. Would ya know it, the jerks still beat one of my patrol officers to death. This made me realize that I had a lot to learn. Trying to manage a safe, monitarily profitable prison is gratifying if you are able to achieve said goal. I've had a lot of fun trying to maintain profits and prison ratings. I've also had fun building a failure and watching my prisoners erupt with anger.
Overall, I have had a great time with this one. I picked it up for cheap during the Summer Sale and I'm happy I pulled the trigger.
*If you are just starting, don't forget that you can close the intake of prisoners. This will save your butt if you are in a race against time.
*Once you have a steady population, don't run the game on the quickest time setting!

Progressing in Terraria naturally unlocks new NPCs that the player can interact with to help them on their adventure! Overall, if you enjoy sandbox-type games with great combat mechanics and the open-ended potential to construct massive structures, then Terraria will definitely be your type of game!

There is a lot to the game of Rust, so I'm going to split this review into sections. 1: Positives. 2: Negatives. 3: Future.
Positives
- Large community with many resources available to help out new players scattered across the internet as well as a Reddit dedicated to people looking for people to play with
- Solid and well polished game play with few noticeable bugs
- Absolutely beautiful landscape
- Infinite replayability due to the fact that Rust is a multiplayer sandbox game
- Easy to understand building and crafting system
- Skill based combat system with learnable recoil in the style of Counter Strike: Global Offensive
- New progression system that ensures players can't immediately hit end-game (This helps the life of servers)
- New progression system also allows for progress to be carried over through wipes, further extending server life
- Forced server wipes every month, resetting all progress and starting back from scratch (Servers get to individually chose if they would rather wipe more frequently)
- Player interaction is frequently hilarious and completely uncontrolled by moderators (Unless by server specific rules)
- The new progression system promotes player interaction more than the last one did
- Facepunch is very good about banning exploiters as soon as they pop up
- Facepunch also listens to suggestions and other actually useful feedback
- Progress is continuous with new game updates being released every Thursday
- Difficulty is determined by other players and server specific rules
Negatives
- The community is in general rather toxic. The majority of players do not interact at all and would prefer to kill other players on sight. That said, the few that do interact make it worth it and it almost always results in a good laugh
- Rust is not fully optimized yet, so lower end computers will have trouble running the game on anything other than the lowest graphics settings
- Playing alone sucks. Some people enjoy it somehow, but I find it's not fun without at least a couple people to play with because everybody else will always outperform you. The Reddit feed I mentioned earlier is a great place to remedy that
- Rust is HARD. Modded servers make it easier for those looking for a more casual take on Rust, but in general the game is very difficult due to the kill on sight nature of most players
Future
Long story short, Rust is still in early access. It has been for years and I find that this is much more of a blessing than a curse. Many people disagree and would prefer a finished product, but the fact that it is still in early access means the developers (Facepunch) are still working on it actively and are taking feedback from their community. This leads to a better end result and a far more enjoyable experience with many new things to try out and give feedback on as development continues. There is a lot planned for the game of Rust as you can see on their website
under the roadmap tab. I urge you to try the game when it goes on sale. It's not everybody's cup of tea, but I believe I can safely say it is one of the best multiplayer survival sandbox games around.

What you'd expect from a worthy Mad Max game.
- Open world post-apocalyptic scenario which blends exploration, car combat and melee combat? check
- Car combat with amazing explosions and deaths? check
- The most satisfying melee combat I've ever seen in a game with grapples, wall executions and counters? check
- Lots of customization and upgrades for Max, his cars and strongolds? check
- Hundreds of unlocks and collectibles? check
- 70s muscle car goodness? check
- Lots of action and destruction? check
- People eating maggots and dog food to survive? check
- Guns and bullets being scarce but a single shot fired can be a game changer on an uphill battle? check
- Game being so well optimized that it runs at 4k60 ultra on a GTX 1060? check
- Max being as badass as they come? check
Of course the game has its cons:
- Steering control gets stuck and unresponsive at times, which can lead you crashing into a canyon for a quick demise, which can be frustrating.
- Aiming can be quite frustrating, and slowing down time doesn't help if the game slows down your aim in an attemp to assist you.
- Game still has many bugs as of November 2017.
All and all for its current price it's a definitive steal. This is the Mad Max game I've always dreamed about.
I highly recommend it unless you're tired of open world games.

I actually dislike most of the action (adventure) games like God Of War and Devil May Cry. They're usually all about the combat, which becomes a boring aspect for me a few hours into the game. And yes, they have great visuals most of the times, but visuals isn't a key aspect for me. Then again; they do help to pull the player into the game world.
Anyway, DmC managed to surprise me because of it's environments, fluent combat and, maybe even more important for me; short campaign. You read correctly, a short campaign. It will take a player somewhere between 7,5-12 hours to fully complete one playthrough, which is a decent length and for me long enough to not become boring or overstay its welcome.
The new Dante starts off as an annoying, run-of-the-mill character. But along the way I started caring for him. He grew more mature it seemed.
Dante will start the game with some basic weaponry and will get new moves and weapons until late in the game, which keeps the combat fresh. Obviously, all weapons and moves can be upgraded. And there really are some amazing moves in there. Using a controller I was able to pull off some of the hardest combos. I'll admit, there was some button mashing involved, but most of the times I actually knew what I was doing.
The environments steal the show though. Rarely have I seen environments this brilliant. The TV show (including boss fight) and nightclub levels are some of the best levels I've ever seen in a game. DmC uses a variety of bright colors, while still having a certain gothic feel to it. It's exceptional.
You can tell they put some real love into the PC version since it will never dip below 60FPS. On Ultra settings things look (mostly) sharp and seeing the game in motion is a real treat, especially during the acrobatic (non-)combat sequences.
The voice acting is top notch, but, unfortunately, the story is a bit on the light side.
Time to wrap things up: I had a great time with this game and I would gladly recommend it to all serious gamers out there.

First of all ignore all the overblown hatred and controversy surrounding the reboot of this much loved classic franchise, because the fact is that it's truly a very good game. Whether it is a positive addition to the DMC franchise or a worthy sucessor to the brand name remains debatable, but in my opinion it is. New Dante (Donte lol) is actually very likeable and develops reasonably as the story progresses unlike what many have feared and the characterization + voice acting/motion capture are absolutely top notch in this game. Combat may not be as deep as some previous entries in the series (ala DMC3) but is still reasonably complex and very, very satisfying. Comboing has never been this smooth and easy. The game does a good job of retaining the inherent combat depth the series is well known for while also making it more accessible for new comers.
The story, which has always been a weak point of the DMC franchise, isn't Oscar worthy but is definitely not something to scoff at. It does a great job of rebooting the story with a very interesting twist on the lore and background of the main chracters. And wrapped up in one of the best visual styles I have ever seen in any game, the game is just pure fun to play through. Ninja Theory really hit the ball out of the park with this one.

Prison Architect is a game that, after a short learning period, I have come to really enjoy. It isn't perfect by any means, and there is a lot of room for improvement. Contructing intricate building can be cumbersome and frustrating. Keeping your prisoners from rioting can be stressful. I can say in full confidence that the enjoyable aspects of prisoner architect far outweigh the drawbacks. I am still relatively new to the game, and I am eager to learn parts of the game that I haven't yet experienced. I've had a chance to check out some community prisons and it is truly incredible what you can build in this game!
In Prison Architect, you play as an omnipotent being. You have the power to plan your prison, hire staff, and allocate prisoners to a living space. At first, you will likely build a quaint holding cell, surrounded by supplemental facilities. Over time, you will have the opportunity to build intricate cell blocks, classrooms, chapels, visitation centers, parole offices, canteens, administrative buildings, and much, much more. Building your prison is where the fun begins.
The game really takes off when it comes to managing your prison. Do you want to run a luxury prison or do you want to rule with an iron fist? Do you want to build a resort or a Gulag? Are you okay with daily bathroom shankings, or do you want all your prisoners and staff to be as safe as possible? I have found that in my earlier stages, I was stressing to keep my prisoners happy. This caused me to indulge my inmates with luxurious prison cells, fully equipped with personal showers and computer desks. Would ya know it, the jerks still beat one of my patrol officers to death. This made me realize that I had a lot to learn. Trying to manage a safe, monitarily profitable prison is gratifying if you are able to achieve said goal. I've had a lot of fun trying to maintain profits and prison ratings. I've also had fun building a failure and watching my prisoners erupt with anger.
Overall, I have had a great time with this one. I picked it up for cheap during the Summer Sale and I'm happy I pulled the trigger.
*If you are just starting, don't forget that you can close the intake of prisoners. This will save your butt if you are in a race against time.
*Once you have a steady population, don't run the game on the quickest time setting!

Just a short vignette game about a bad night out

This is a short illustrated story that depicts a single night in one person's life. It takes about 10 minutes to read through.
The writing is good and the pacing is perfect. The visuals and audio work well to set the mood and convey emotion.
There is no twist, punchline or moral; no tragedy, triumph or deep philosophical revelation. Anyone can have a night like this, and many people do. Maybe you did too. This is only an opportunity to see the world through someone else's eyes and share their experience. It might lead you to think, feel and understand. And if not, hey, it's only 10 minutes.

Making you feel powerless, this free five-minute painted point-and-click short story of a typical young woman's night out highlights how a low regard for and high level of objectification of women are all too often considered acceptable.
To those who are saying that this game is condoning such behaviour, you are responding emotionally as it intends, but missing that we are being shown the way things are, not the way they should be.
As a side note, while not obscene, this game is not for children. I hope Steam and other online distribution platforms come to implement age verification more thoroughly in the case of free games.

People having been saying for quite some time that Super Meat Boy is a fantatstic game because its difficulty makes it fun, but it goes too far. Don't think that i'm egging you on or anything, im not giving you a challange by saying it's too hard, i'm trying to stop you from buying it. The levels are difficult to the point where you simply have to try them, over, and over, and over, and over again. I understand the desire to return to a time when videogames were challenging, but what people don't understand is that the challange never went away, all you have to do is put the game on hard mode, which nearly every game has. A good game will give the option to be difficult, and when it is difficult it will provide you a challange that requires you to be more carefull and thoughtfull. Super Meat Boy forces the game to be extremely difficult and the only way to beat it is to try it again, and again, and again, essentailly a kind of difficulty where repitition matters more than thought, I wouldn't accept those kinds of conditions in a job, so why in the world should I want them in something I do for fun!? Do yourself a favor, but Battle Block Theater, a game with an OPTIONAL yet still very challanging hard mode, a hilarious and well thought out story, as well as more interesting mechanics, and multiplayer.

What you'd expect from a worthy Mad Max game.
- Open world post-apocalyptic scenario which blends exploration, car combat and melee combat? check
- Car combat with amazing explosions and deaths? check
- The most satisfying melee combat I've ever seen in a game with grapples, wall executions and counters? check
- Lots of customization and upgrades for Max, his cars and strongolds? check
- Hundreds of unlocks and collectibles? check
- 70s muscle car goodness? check
- Lots of action and destruction? check
- People eating maggots and dog food to survive? check
- Guns and bullets being scarce but a single shot fired can be a game changer on an uphill battle? check
- Game being so well optimized that it runs at 4k60 ultra on a GTX 1060? check
- Max being as badass as they come? check
Of course the game has its cons:
- Steering control gets stuck and unresponsive at times, which can lead you crashing into a canyon for a quick demise, which can be frustrating.
- Aiming can be quite frustrating, and slowing down time doesn't help if the game slows down your aim in an attemp to assist you.
- Game still has many bugs as of November 2017.
All and all for its current price it's a definitive steal. This is the Mad Max game I've always dreamed about.
I highly recommend it unless you're tired of open world games.

So what can I say about Prison Architect... this is a tale of a gardener who lost his life in the line of duty.
The tale begins with taking on 26 maximum security convicts which seemed like a good idea at the time, this was my first mistake... these convicts proceed to cause mayhem across my entire prison so I hire extra guards while the armed guards were being researched.
As I expand the prison I hire 2 gardeners, and a few janitors who carried on as normal throughout the entire prison outbreak... armed guard research is finally done and I have them patrolling the canteen and cells of the max security convicts, this became my second mistake. A prison riot broke out and I found my poor defenceless gardener beaten to death by around 6 or 7 convicts in a corner and to add insult to injury he was then taken to the morgue and later removed by a guard who decided the garbage bay should be his final resting place.
While all of this ensues the canteen seems to have broken out in a fight, armed guards should be able to handle this right? Wrong, apparently one of the convicts managed to take the shotgun from the guards to which I locked the canteen down with everyone inside... the convict slaughtered every single person in that building except one lone cook who continued making meals throughout the entire ordeal... rumour has it hes still cooking to this day.
As for the convict with the shotgun a single badass guard came out of nowhere clothlined him and beat him unconcious before taking him to solitary confinement.
These events didn't seem to phase my army of janitors who once the doors reopened swept through cleaning around the layers and layers of bodies which now littered the canteen floors, at least they kept going... its what the gardener would have wanted.
After the events of dark Wednesday I am honestly not sure which is going to be harder repairing and cleaning up the mess or explaining all this to the gardeners family...

As it is now, Arkham City is the best game in the series (I guess I should say, In My Humble Opinion). Arkham Origins was an unfortunate step backwards... possibly even two steps. I'm actually afraid to run out and buy Arkham Knight because of the possibility of another disappointment. I'll spare everyone (and myself) a long drawn out explanation. There are plenty of reviewers who have gone over the bad--at length. I agree with a lot the "Not Recommended" posters and here's one reason: The leap the Batman Arkham series made from Asylum to City was huge in terms of graphics, story, gameplay, etc. The unfortunately is no leap, no improvement, but actually regression when moving from City to Origins.
Basically, aside from the bugs that plagued Origins (even making some "boss" battles come completely to a halt), the story, characters, graphics, and gameplay are all subpar compared to Arkham City. Yes I've logged 60+ hours playing this game, but that is mostly playing the challenges to beat my high scores. They are far more entertaining than the story mode.
**Potential Spoilers**
The cast of characters, the roles they play, and how they all make their appearances is expertly executed in Arkham City (Clayface and Ra's al Ghul in particular). Characters in Arkham Origins, like Killer Croc, just come and go haphazardly with no shock, suspense, or sense of belonging. Many character appearances and interactions are flat, disjointed, and add no real value to the "story". Compare Mad Hatter's appearance in Arkham City to his appearance in Arkham Origins. The execution in Arkham City is leagues better and what!? the Mad Hatter's appearance actually ties in with the story. Arkham City's all-star cast of characters from the Batman/Gotham universe enhance the game's story and provide actual thrills, plot twists, and an overall cinematic experience.
**End Potential Spoilers**
The only character that Arkham Origins in better at is the Joker. Arkham Origins does do a good job of portraying the more sadistic, homicidal side of the Joker. Arkham City's Joker is the more soft, comical, PG-rated animated series version. Arkham Origins has a pretty good Gordon too. Speaking of which, the story does a decent job of portraying the corruption within the GCPD. It reminds me of how the corruption is portrayed in Batman Year One (the animated feature). It's pretty well done.

It's difficult to write a review for a game like Super Meat Boy, specifically beacause my opinion about this game might get judged and banalized up to a point where it might not make any sense whatsoever for this review to ever exist, this could even be the glaring review that would affect the general perseption of different people (including myself) about me, but so be it.
Super Meat Boy it's a fantastic game, however, it's one of the most punishing and crushingly difficult games that i've ever played, i've played them all, you mention it, Contra, i played it, Battletoads, played it, Metal Slug in the arcades, played it, Castlevania, i could go on this list for hours till end and bring up big names in the industry with their own respective respect and ambision that was gladly achieved in plenty of cases (such as the ones that i mentioned before) but there was a difference back then and there' s a difference now, i never condoned this game as the best specifically because of the questionable and debatable (at best) level of difficulty, those games where built around it under an "arcade mentality", as i liked to call it, back then it was not understandable, the only reason why people liked those games was because they were made in a time where that was the only things that you would get, difficulty, and creativity, all mixed into one.
Super Meat Boy takes a different route on this, it tries to be a fish out the sea in modern gaming, and despite succeeding in a tremendous way, the game still holds a place into the deliberetly punishment that it's a developer obsessed with nostalgia and "old games" up to a point where he decides to make it's own using similar, if not exact mechanics as the ones used before, the game doesn't stand still on it's feet when it comes to difficulty the first prump recommends you to use a gamepad, and the entire game has "laggy" controls, when in a game like this precision is key to the player's success.
It's difficult to not "recommend" this game, i wish there was a way where i could stand in the clear and just tell you mi view about this game but there isnt' and despite what some might say i just have to go with the way that i feel, this game is not recommended by me, because i think i could get much more worthwhile, meningful, and thoughtful experiences with the money i spended on Super Meat Boy.
